buildings.summary: Buildings are the weakest art in the frame. `RoofLayer.drawTops` re-issues ~25 vector ops per building per frame (no view culling at all — every building on a 320x240 map is iterated every frame), and the result is a flat two-tone slab: one `fillRect` per slope, gable triangles, 0.4 m course hairlines, a `rgba(255,235,210,0.35)` ridge line that reads as programmer art, one 0.35 m chimney square, and 2-3 dark flecks on roofs over 45 m². Nothing about the roof is baked, so per-shingle texture, moss, dormers and damage are currently unaffordable. Two structural problems compound it: (1) the terracotta palette is the most saturated thing in the game — `#8a4b37` tinted x1.22 +9 warmth gives a lit slope at ~67% saturation against a world capped near 35%, which is exactly the "toy" read the audit flagged; (2) `FADE_SCALE = 14` means every roof drops to 0.12 alpha above 14 px/m, so at the sweep's own village/farm crop scale (24 px/m, `scripts/lib/stage.mjs` `deriveTargets`) the art the player actually sees in tactical play is a ghost — the base screenshots only look opaque because `place()` settles just two frames and the alpha lerp (`dt*6`) has only reached ~0.84. Buildings also have zero mass (no wall face, no parallax, hard-edged rect shadows) and sit in raw grass with no yard, wall, gate or garden, so a Normandy village reads as coloured rectangles dropped on a lawn. The fix is a bake: three sprites per building per zoom band (ground shadow / wall+openings / roof), which makes shingle courses, materials, dormers, weathering and damage holes free at frame time while dropping the frame cost below what it is today.

tasks.title: Recalibrate roof palette and value structure (desaturate terracotta, kill the white ridge hairline)
tasks.detail: Standalone constants-only pass that lands before the bake and immediately removes the toy read. In roofs.ts: replace `PALETTES = ['#8a4b37','#77503c','#5a5e65']` with a material table (consumed by B2) whose bases sit inside the muted ceiling — tuile `#6f4a3c` (111,74,60 → S 46%), weathered tuile `#6b5342`, ardoise slate `#565b62` (S 6%), cool slate `#4e565e`. In `buildArt`, drop the lit tint from `tint(weathered, 1.22, 9)` to `tint(weathered, 1.14, 5)` and shade from `0.7,-9` to `0.72,-7`; keep the lit/shade value ratio near 1.6 (value separation is the legibility mechanism per architecture.md rule 1 — do NOT flatten it, only pull hue). Verify the lit slope stays under ~50% saturation: (111*1.14+5, 74*1.14, 60*1.14-5) = (132,84,63) → S 52%, acceptable as the frame's single warm accent. Gable tint `0.5,-12` → `0.55,-9` (current gable ends read as near-black notches at 8 px/m). Replace the ridge stroke `rgba(255,235,210,0.35)` with `rgba(214,203,186,0.28)` and widen to 0.14 (B2 replaces it with real ridge caps, but this makes the interim frame look right). Drop the course-line alpha from 0.14 to 0.10 and vary it per building via `hash(i, 200)` in ±0.03 so courses stop reading as a printed grid. Widen `valueJitter` from ±6% to ±9% and `hueJitter` from ±8 to ±11 so two adjacent tile roofs never match. Re-run `node scripts/sweep.mjs` and compare the village/hamlet columns against .screenshots/sweep for saturation only — no geometry should move.
tasks.risks: Pulling saturation too far makes tile and slate converge; guard by checking the two materials stay >=15 value points apart on the lit slope. The sweep contact sheet is the only regression gate — every crop with a building changes, so review the whole village/hamlet/farm column, not one image.

tasks.title: Bake roof sprites per (building, zoom band) with slate/tile/thatch/corrugated materials, shingle courses, ridge caps and weathering
tasks.detail: The enabler for every other roof task. Add a bake layer inside roofs.ts (or split src/render/roofbake.ts): `ROOF_BANDS = [8, 16, 32]` (px/m; no 48 band — roofs are alpha<=0.18 above B3's fade threshold, so a 32 px/m bake downscaled is invisible loss), `roofBandFor(scale)` mirroring `bandFor` in dudes.ts. Cache `Map<number /*band*/, (HTMLCanvasElement|null)[]>`; on band change keep serving the previously baked band (scaled) and enqueue rebakes, so there is no pop and no fallback vector path. Amortize: `BAKES_PER_FRAME = 2` (same amortization pattern as the logged order-burst decision) plus a prewarm loop during the paused boot frame. Sprite geometry: per building store `{ox, oy, ow, oh}` in world meters = footprint expanded by OVERHANG + `padNW 0.35` (dormer/lean-to spill, B5) + `padSE 0.35`; bake canvas `(ow*band, oh*band)`, `g.scale(band, band)`, `g.translate(-ox, -oy)` so all bake code is written in the same world-meter units as today's draw code. Frame loop in `drawTops` becomes: view-cull against `cam.worldToScreen` (currently absent — every building on the map draws every frame), `ctx.globalAlpha = a`, one `ctx.drawImage(spr, ox, oy, ow, oh)` inside the existing `withWorldTransform`. Materials: `type RoofMat = 'tile'|'slate'|'thatch'|'iron'` chosen in `buildArt` from `hash(i, 201)` biased by footprint and story count — `sim.map.storiesAt` >=2 (footprint >=56 tiles, see addBuilding in mapgen.ts) never gets thatch; a building whose nearest neighbour footprint is within 4 m and which is the smaller of the pair (the mapgen farm house+barn pair) gets thatch/iron at 70%. Per-material bake: tile = courses of `COURSE=0.34` m from eave to ridge, per course a 50%-staggered run of `TILE_W=0.30` m fillRects with value from `hash(i, 210 + course*97 + t)` at ±7%, a `rgba(0,0,0,0.13)` butt line 0.035 m at each course bottom, and every ~9th tile swapped to a patched tone (`tint(base, 0.86, +6)`); slate = `COURSE=0.24`, `TILE_W=0.22`, tighter ±4% jitter, cooler patch tone, plus a few `rgba(232,238,244,0.10)` specular flecks (wet slate); thatch = no courses — instead 0.06 m combed streaks running down-slope every 0.12 m with `hash`-varied length/value, a 0.5 m-deep rounded eave (arcTo corners, not roundRect, to stay engine-version independent) and a fat 0.34 m ridge roll with a dark spar band and cross-ties every 0.5 m; iron = 0.28 m ribs down-slope, alternating light/dark 0.04 m lines, plus 2-4 rust bleeds (`rgba(122,74,44,0.22)` soft ellipses) from the ridge. Band-adaptive detail (required by the zoom-band rule): at band 8 skip per-tile fills entirely and draw courses + 3-tile-wide coarse value blocks; per-tile geometry only at band >=16. Ridge caps replace the hairline: half-round caps of 0.33 m along the ridge with a 0.02 m gap — mid-tone body 0.18 m tall, `rgba(226,214,196,0.22)` 0.05 m lit strip on the NW side, `rgba(18,15,12,0.35)` 0.05 m on the SE side. Weathering pass (all `hash(i, 220+)`): 2-4 moss blobs (soft radial gradient, `rgba(96,112,64,0.30)`) biased to the SE slope's eave third and to the chimney/valley junctions; 1-2 course-aligned patch rectangles (whole runs of 3-6 tiles in the patched tone, not the current free-floating 0.25 m squares — replace `art.flecks`); 2-3 vertical drip stains below the ridge on the SE slope (`rgba(30,26,20,0.14)`, 0.08 m wide, length 0.3-0.6 of the slope); occasional 2-3 missing tiles at one eave corner (dark `#211d17` gaps). Legibility guard: bake the eave outline as a `1.3/band` metre stroke so it survives downscale, and in `drawTops` stroke a separate per-frame `rgba(20,16,12,0.55)` footprint outline at `max(a, 0.45)` alpha so a faded roof still shows the wall line (the interior-reveal state must never lose the building silhouette).
tasks.risks: Bake hitch if amortization is skipped — a 12x7 m roof at band 16 is ~850 fillRects; 25 buildings baked in one frame is a visible stall. Memory is not a concern (~9 MB/band for 25 buildings) but MUST drop non-current bands or it grows x3. Per-tile jitter above ±8% fizzes into noise when downscaled from band 32 to 16 px/m — check the sweep at scale 24 before committing amplitudes. All roof hash salts must stay >=200: 60-82 are already taken by buildArt.

tasks.title: Retune the roof fade so the roof art is visible in tactical play
tasks.detail: Cheapest multiplier on every other task here: today `FADE_SCALE = 14` drops EVERY roof to 0.12 alpha above 14 px/m, and 24-32 px/m is the normal tactical range (the sweep's own village/farm crops are 24). All of B1/B2/B5/B6's work is invisible there. Preserve both hooks, change the trigger set: (1) raise `FADE_SCALE` to 26 so pure-zoom reveal only fires at the close inspection band; (2) make occupancy the primary trigger and extend it to any soldier the player can already see, matching the rule upper floors already use — replace the `s.level > 0 ? sim.soldierVisibleTo('blue', s) : s.side === 'blue'` split with `sim.soldierVisibleTo('blue', s)` for all levels (this leaks nothing: it is gated on the sim's own visibility helper, and the renderer still never re-derives vision); (3) raise the faded floor from 0.12 to 0.18 and keep B2's full-alpha footprint outline so a revealed building still reads as a building; (4) leave `interiorVisibleAt`'s `< 0.5` threshold and the `dt*6` lerp alone — terrain.ts `drawStairs` depends on that exact semantic. Also widen the fade to a 2 px/m hysteresis band (fade in above 26, restore below 24) so scroll-wheel zoom near the threshold does not flicker the whole village.
tasks.risks: This is a feel/UX change, not purely art — get sign-off. Extending occupancy fade to visible enemies means an enemy-garrisoned house you have eyes on opens its roof; that is consistent with the existing upper-floor rule but changes what the player reads at a glance. Raising FADE_SCALE also means interiors stay hidden longer, so verify room clearing at 20-24 px/m still feels playable with occupancy fade doing the work.

tasks.title: Baked base sprite: soft-blurred one-sun shadow, NW parallax, and stone/half-timber wall faces with real windows
tasks.detail: Buildings currently have zero mass: `drawShadows` stamps two hard-edged offset rects plus an AO strokeRect, and the roof covers footprint+OVERHANG exactly so no wall is ever visible. Bake two more sprites per (building, band), same origin/size struct as B2 so one `blit(i, spr)` helper serves all three. SHADOW sprite (drawn in `drawShadows`, alpha still multiplied by `this.alphas[i]` so a faded roof strands no stain): pad SE by `shadowOffset(1.1 * stories)` + 0.6 m blur margin; fill the roof silhouette polygon (including B5's wing/lean-to and B6's chimney, so the shadow matches the object) with `rgba(12,15,10,SHADOW_SOFT_ALPHA)` at the long offset under `g.filter = 'blur(' + (0.28*band) + 'px)'`, then the core at `shadowOffset(0.71*stories)` with `blur(0.12*band)` and `SHADOW_ALPHA`, then `g.filter='none'` and the unblurred contact AO ring at `AO_ALPHA` on the true footprint. ctx.filter is a Chrome bake-time nicety — if unsupported the assignment is a no-op and edges just stay hard, so no guard needed, but note it. WALL sprite (new pass called right after `drawShadows`, before soldiers, always alpha 1 — walls exist whether or not the roof is faded): introduce a fake-oblique parallax so the SE wall face shows. Draw the roof sprite offset by `-SUN * PARALLAX` where `PARALLAX = 0.18` m (B2's blit origin shifts; because OVERHANG is 0.35 the footprint stays fully covered on all four sides, so the wall-line read gameplay depends on is unchanged), and project the wall face outward from the S and E footprint edges by `H_PROJ = 0.5 * stories` metres. Wall materials from `hash(i, 260)`: limestone rubble `#9a9285` with 0.45 m block value jitter and `rgba(60,54,44,0.35)` mortar ticks; colombage half-timber = pale cob `#a89e86` panels with `#4a3c2c` timber uprights every 0.7 m plus one mid rail; brick `#7d5a4a` with 0.22 m courses (rare, ~15%). Openings are data-driven, not decorative: scan `sim.map.hEdge(x, b.y+b.h)` and `sim.map.vEdge(b.x+b.w, y)` across the footprint and for each `EDGE.WINDOW` draw a 0.6 m dark `#39424a` pane with a `rgba(226,214,190,0.35)` sill line and a `#3a3128` frame, for each `EDGE.DOOR` a taller `#5f4426` leaf — mapgen puts windows at `i % 3 === 1` and the door mid-span, so this lines up with what terrain.ts already strokes on the edges. Top the wall face with a 0.10 m `rgba(14,12,9,0.4)` eave-shadow strip (belongs to the roof, so bake it into the ROOF sprite's SE edge, not the wall sprite) and bottom it with a 0.08 m `rgba(10,12,8,0.45)` base line. Add `export const WIND = { dx: 0.82, dy: -0.57 }` to light.ts (one wind, like one sun — B6 and any later grass/flag motion share it).
tasks.risks: The 0.5 m/story wall projection extends outside the footprint into walkable tiles, so a soldier standing hard against the south wall overlaps it; drawing the wall sprite under soldiers makes that read as 'in front of the wall', which is correct for an NW-oblique view, but keep H_PROJ <= 0.5/story or it starts looking like a sim/art mismatch. 2-story buildings project 1.0 m — check against the mapgen minimum 4-tile building depth. Do not let the parallax offset exceed OVERHANG or the roof will uncover the footprint's NW edge and break the wall-line read.

tasks.title: Roof plan variety: hip, cross-gable, catslide and lean-to, plus dormers on the sun slope
tasks.detail: Every roof in the game is the same centred gable over a rectangle, which is why a village reads as cloned. Footprints come from the sim and must not change; vary the roof PLAN inside them. In `buildArt` add `plan` from `hash(i, 240)` gated on footprint aspect: `gable` (current, ~35%); `hip` (~25%) — ridge along the long axis but inset from both ends by `min(h/2, 1.8)` m, giving two trapezoid main slopes plus two end slopes drawn at an intermediate value (`tint(weathered, 0.92, 0)` for the NE end, `0.80` for the SW) so four planes read distinctly; `cross-gable` (~20%, only when `min(w,h) >= 6`) — main ridge plus a perpendicular wing over a hash-chosen 30-45% span of the long axis at the same ridge height, drawn after the main planes with a `rgba(16,14,10,0.30)` 0.10 m valley line along each intersection; `catslide` (~20%) — ridge offset to 0.40/0.60 of the span so one slope is long and shallow, and extend that side's eave by an extra 0.25 m (the classic Normandy lean-to read). Lean-to annex: on ~30% of buildings add a 1.4-2.2 m deep shed roof against one non-door wall, ridge-less, single plane sloping away from the wall, 0.35 m lower than the main eave with its own eave outline and its own shadow contribution — bake into the same sprite, extend `padSE`/`padNW` accordingly. Dormers: when the NW slope depth >= 2.2 m and footprint area >= 45, place 1-3 dormers on the NW (sun) slope at `hash(i, 250+k)` positions along the ridge with a 1.6 m minimum gap, each a 1.1 m wide x 0.8 m deep gabled box — small two-plane roof in the parent material, a `#39424a` window pane with a lit sill, a `rgba(14,12,9,0.35)` SE cast shadow onto the main slope offset by `shadowOffset(0.5)`, and a 0.06 m valley line where the cheeks meet the slope. Barns/iron roofs get a ridge vent instead (a 0.25 m raised strip with dark louvre ticks) plus one 0.5 m roof hatch. At band 8 draw dormers as a simple 2-tone block (the window and sill are sub-pixel there) — again band-adaptive, not band-fighting. All of this is bake-time only, so frame cost is unchanged.
tasks.risks: Cross-gable wings and lean-tos push geometry past the footprint; the sprite pad and the B4 shadow silhouette must both grow or you get clipped roofs and shadows that do not match. Hip ends shorten the ridge, so B6's ridge-end chimney placement must clamp to the inset ridge. Keep every plan's outer boundary a superset of the footprint so the gameplay wall-line read never degrades.

tasks.title: Chimney upgrade with roof-clipped shadow, plus drifting smoke wisps on the shared wind
tasks.detail: Baked half: replace the single `fillRect` + `strokeRect` chimney with a stack that has mass. Body 0.50 x 0.40 m in `#4a4038` with a 0.14 m SE side face at `tint x0.72` (same fake-oblique as B4's walls); a cap slab overhanging 0.06 m on all sides with a `rgba(226,214,196,0.28)` 0.04 m lit NW top edge and a `rgba(12,10,8,0.45)` SE underline; 1-2 pot circles (`#2a241e`, r 0.07 m) with a soot ring; brick/limestone course ticks from `hash(i, 270+)`. Cast shadow: a parallelogram from the stack footprint offset by `shadowOffset(1.2)` (chimney ~1.2 m above the roof plane), filled `rgba(14,12,9,0.38)` and CLIPPED to the roof polygon so it never spills onto the ground — the current code draws a square shadow that can hang off the eave. Placement: Normandy chimneys sit at gable ends, so bias the along-ridge parameter `t` to 0.06-0.20 or 0.80-0.94 at 70% (`hash(i, 271)`), mid-ridge otherwise, clamped inside a hipped roof's inset ridge (B5); footprint area >= 70 gets a second stack at the opposite end. Dynamic half: `RoofLayer.drawChimneySmoke(ctx, cam, cw, ch)`, called from `Renderer.draw` immediately after `this.roofs.drawTops(...)` and before `this.drawSmoke(...)` so sim smoke composites over it. Smoking set = `hash(i, 272) < 0.45`, houses only (never iron/barn). Gate on `cam.scale >= 6` (at far LOD hundreds of chimneys would fizz) and on the existing on-screen pad test idiom from `drawSmoke`. Phase from `this.sim.tick / 30` (30 ticks/s — same basis as `barrageMarks`), never `now`, so wisps freeze under pause exactly like sim smoke does. Per chimney 3-4 puffs: `life = ((tick/30) * 0.45 + i/n + hash(i, 273+i)) % 1`, position = chimney top + `WIND * (life * 3.2)` (from light.ts, added in B4) + a cross-wind sine wobble of amplitude `0.25 * life`, radius `0.18 + life * 0.7`, fill `rgba(196,190,178, 0.20 * (1-life) * roofAlpha_i)` — multiply by the building's roof alpha so a revealed interior does not get smoke floating over it. That is ~32 arcs/frame at a typical village view: negligible.
tasks.risks: Smoke is hash-driven ambience, not occupancy-driven, so it leaks no intel — but do not later tie it to garrison state without thinking about fog of war. Puffs drawn above roofs will pass over adjacent buildings' roofs; keep alpha <= 0.20 so it reads as haze, not as a sprite ordering bug. Clipping the chimney shadow needs the roof polygon path retained from B5's plan code — build the polygon once per bake and reuse.

tasks.title: Yards: garden walls, picket fences, gates aligned to doors, door aprons, kitchen gardens, farmyard clutter
tasks.detail: Biggest single win outside the roof itself: buildings currently sit in undifferentiated grass, which is what makes the village read as rectangles on a lawn. All of it goes in the terrain chunk bake (frame cost zero). In `TerrainLayer`'s constructor, derive footprints once by scanning `map.buildingId` (O(w*h), same pass style as the existing `hasElev`/`hasStairs` probes) into `{id, x, y, w, h, doorSide}`; doorSide comes from scanning the footprint perimeter for `EDGE.DOOR` via `map.hEdge`/`map.vEdge`. Critical implementation detail: iterate BUILDINGS BY BOUNDS, not tiles — for each chunk, draw every footprint whose bounds expanded by `YARD_REACH = 6` m intersect the chunk's padded rect. The existing `pad = 2` overscan is not enough reach, and because every op is deterministic world-space and both neighbouring chunks paint identical pixels in their shared gutter, cross-chunk features stay seamless (same property trees already rely on). Call order inside `chunk()`: tile bases → yard ground (apron, garden rows, farmyard mud) → `drawDoorTrails` (so trails wear over the gravel) → yard structures (walls/fences, which have shadows) → `drawHedgeRun` → trees → `drawEdge`. Content, all `hash(id, 0, 300+)` keyed so a building's yard is stable and no two match: (1) Yard boundary on the door side, 3-5 m deep, wall or fence from `hash(id,0,300)`. Wall = 0.32 m capsule stroke in limestone `#9a9285` with 0.45 m block value jitter and mortar ticks, built with the exact 4-pass idiom `drawHedgeRun` already uses — AO at `AO_ALPHA*0.6`, soft shadow at `shadowOffset(0.5)*1.6`, core shadow at `shadowOffset(0.5)`, mass, then a `rgba(214,206,186,0.22)` NW rim; capstones every 0.5 m. Fence = 0.10 m posts every 1.2 m plus two 0.05 m rails, each with its own SE shadow. Always leave a 1.3 m gate gap centred on the door, with two gate posts and (50%) a `#5f4426` open leaf swung along the wind side. (2) Door apron: 2.0 x 1.6 m of gravel/cobble — 14-20 ellipses 0.18-0.26 m in three warm-grey tones over a `rgba(150,140,120,0.35)` base, clipped away from any `terrainKeyAt === 'road'` tile so it never paints over the arterial. (3) Kitchen garden on the side opposite the door when the ground there is grass: 2.5 x 3 m of 4-6 dark furrow rows (`rgba(58,46,32,0.30)`, 0.09 m) with 5-9 cabbage dots (`#4c5c38` circles r 0.14 m) and a couple of bean-pole ticks. (4) Farmyard: when two footprints are within 5 m (the mapgen house+barn pair), fill the gap with beaten earth — overlapping `rgba(120,102,74,0.4)` ellipses plus two wheel ruts — and add a dung heap (dark `#4a3a26` mound with straw ticks), a woodpile against the barn's SE wall (a 1.6 x 0.5 m stack of 0.16 m log-end circles in two tones), a water trough, and at 30% a cart (two 0.4 m wheels plus a shaft). (5) Ivy: 3-5 `rgba(52,68,40,0.5)` blobs hugging one wall corner. Never paint inside a footprint (interiors must stay clean for room clearing) and skip any tile whose `terrainKeyAt` is road, water or floor.
tasks.risks: Garden walls are visual-only — soldiers and vehicles walk straight through them, an art/sim mismatch. Mitigate by keeping them knee-high in read (0.32 m stroke, low shadow) so 'stepped over' is plausible, and do NOT scale them up to waist height without adding real terrain. Second risk: yard features must not close off the door trail or the tile the sim uses as the door approach — align the gate gap to the door column/row exactly. Third: this multiplies chunk bake cost near villages; measure the first-paint hitch when panning into the village at band 32 and, if it bites, gate clutter (4) and (5) to band >= 16.

tasks.title: Cheap roof damage states driven by real impacts
tasks.detail: The sim has no building HP and must not gain one, but the renderer already receives every detonation: `Renderer.addBooms` (fed by `sim.takeBooms()` in main.ts) stamps `decals.scorch`. Add `this.roofs.noteImpact(b.x, b.y)` on the same line. `RoofLayer.noteImpact` finds the building whose footprint contains the point (or is within 1.5 m), pushes `{x, y}` onto that building's `damage` array (cap 3, ignore points within 0.8 m of an existing entry), and invalidates that building's cached sprites in every band so the next amortized bake redraws it — reuse B2's `BAKES_PER_FRAME` queue so a barrage that hits four houses cannot stall a frame. Direct hit bake (inside the footprint): ragged hole polygon, 9 vertices at radius `0.7 + hash(rx, ry, 290+k) * 0.5` m around the impact (`rx/ry` = impact rounded to 0.25 m so the shape is stable across rebakes), filled `#16130f`; inside it, exposed rafters as `rgba(112,92,64,0.8)` 0.06 m lines every 0.42 m running perpendicular to the ridge with a `rgba(20,16,12,0.7)` shadow line beside each, clipped to the hole path; a rim of 8-14 displaced tiles (parent material, ±25% value, rotated 10-25 degrees) scattered 0.1-0.5 m outside the hole; a `rgba(24,20,16,0.30)` radial soot gradient out to 2x the hole radius. Near miss (within footprint+1.5 m but not inside): soot gradient plus 3-5 cracked/slipped tiles only — no hole. Then register a lazy plume: reuse B6's wisp code with radius `0.4 + life*1.4`, tone `rgba(140,132,120, 0.22*(1-life))` and origin at the hole centre, so a shelled village visibly smokes. Everything is render-only and resets when the buildings list identity changes (`update`'s existing `this.buildings !== sim.buildings` guard), so nothing persists into a new battle unless someone later wires it to the per-cell scar list — do not do that here, it would touch campaign state.
tasks.risks: Purely cosmetic damage on a building that still gives full cover can read as a lie; keep holes to roof planes and never suggest a collapsed wall or a breach the sim will not honour. Rebaking mid-barrage is the one place this can hitch — it must go through the amortized queue, never bake inline in noteImpact. Impact coordinates must be quantized before hashing or the hole shape will shimmer on every rebake.

mobile.summary: Mobile support is zero, and not merely "unstyled" — the game is unplayable on a phone before any polish argument starts. `index.html` has no viewport meta (so mobile browsers render at the 980px legacy layout viewport), the canvas is sized `innerWidth×innerHeight` with no devicePixelRatio handling (`src/main.ts:29-34`), and every world interaction is bound to `mousedown/mousemove/mouseup/contextmenu/wheel` on the canvas plus `keydown` (`src/main.ts:463-793`) — the only Pointer Event in the codebase is the audio unlock at `src/main.ts:100`, which is the one thing that already works on touch. The hard blocker: in strategic mode `hud.root` is hidden (`src/main.ts:838`) and pause/speed exist only as Space and Digit1/2/3, while boot state is `stratPaused = true` (`src/main.ts:82`) — a touch user boots the campaign and can never start the clock. Battle input additionally depends on right-click (order issue), right-drag (formation width/facing), shift (add-to-selection / force-squad-order), alt (floor menu), wheel (the only zoom path), 1-9 (squad select), Shift+1-8 (order kind), and hover (tooltip + order affordance tips) — every one of those needs a touch equivalent. HUD chrome is hard-pixel and desktop-shaped: `#squads` is a 258px left panel whose right edge (266px) the boot-framing logic explicitly measures (`viewportInset`, `src/main.ts:282-299`), `#hint` is two `white-space:nowrap` keyboard-legend spans, `#tip` is 236px mouse-following, `.ord` buttons are ~28×18px, `.st-wp-cancel` is 18×18px, and the strategic view paints a 216px legend + 220px chit panel straight onto the canvas regardless of width. Two incidental findings worth folding in: `sim.queueMove` (the waypoint queue) has zero production callers — only tests — so the HUD's "shift+right-click waypoint" hint and the `squadWaypoints` route overlay are advertising a feature the live game cannot reach; and `PIXEL_BUDGET = 24_000_000` in `src/render/terrain.ts:12` (~96MB RGBA) plus an unbudgeted 300-chunk first-frame bake are the two things most likely to kill a mobile Safari tab.

tasks.title: Viewport meta, DPR-aware canvas sizing, touch-action baseline
tasks.detail:
Foundation for everything else; nothing touch-related works correctly until the coordinate space and the viewport are right.

(1) index.html head: `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover">` and `<meta name="theme-color" content="#1a1d1a">`. Body/canvas CSS in the same inline block: `html,body{height:100%;margin:0;overflow:hidden;overscroll-behavior:none;-webkit-text-size-adjust:100%;-webkit-tap-highlight-color:transparent}` and `canvas{display:block;position:fixed;inset:0;touch-action:none;user-select:none;-webkit-user-select:none;-webkit-touch-callout:none}`. CRITICAL: keep `touch-action:none` scoped to the canvas — a global rule kills scrolling in `#squads`, `#st-chit-panel`, `#pausemenu .db-scroll` and `#debrief .db-scroll`; add `touch-action:pan-y` to those four in ui.css. `-webkit-touch-callout:none` + `user-select:none` on the canvas is load-bearing for M2's press-and-hold (iOS otherwise raises the selection callout mid-gesture).

(2) New `src/render/view.ts`: `export const view = { w: 0, h: 0, dpr: 1 };` plus a pure, testable `export function viewSize(cssW, cssH, rawDpr, maxDpr = 2, maxPx = 2_600_000): {w,h,dpr}` = clamp `dpr` to `[1, maxDpr]`, then `dpr = Math.max(1, Math.min(dpr, Math.sqrt(maxPx / (cssW * cssH))))`. A 3× 390×844 phone is 2.96 Mpx of fill per frame with hundreds of drawImage calls on top — the area cap, not just the 2× cap, is what keeps the frame budget.

(3) `resize()` in main.ts becomes: read `const w = Math.round(visualViewport?.width ?? innerWidth), h = Math.round(visualViewport?.height ?? innerHeight)`; `const v = viewSize(w, h, devicePixelRatio || 1)`; set `canvas.style.width = w+'px'; canvas.style.height = h+'px'; canvas.width = Math.round(w*v.dpr); canvas.height = Math.round(h*v.dpr);` then `ctx.setTransform(v.dpr, 0, 0, v.dpr, 0, 0)` and assign `view.w/h/dpr`. Register `visualViewport?.addEventListener('resize', …)` and `window.addEventListener('orientationchange', …)` alongside the existing `resize`, all coalesced through one rAF-pending flag (iOS fires resize repeatedly while the URL bar collapses).

(4) The whole render/pick pipeline must switch from device px to CSS px. Replace `canvas.width`/`canvas.height` with `view.w`/`view.h` at every main.ts call site: 362, 471, 504, 518-519, 542, 612, 632, 703, 884, 897-898, 914, 916, 924, 975. Replace `ctx.canvas.width/height` with `view.w/view.h` at `src/render/renderer.ts:114-115` and `src/ui/overlays.ts:28-29` (grep confirms those are the only two indirect reads). Because the base transform carries the DPR, every existing constant — `cam.scale` min 2 / max 48, `PAN_PX_PER_SEC = 550`, the `15 / cam.scale` pick radius, `pickAt`'s `12 / cam.scale`, the zoom `1.003^px` curve — keeps its CSS-pixel meaning, which is what makes desktop behavior identical rather than merely similar.

(5) `canvas.getContext('2d', { alpha: false })`. Both modes already clear the full canvas every frame (`renderer.ts:120`, `strategic.ts:92-93`), so an opaque context is behavior-neutral and drops a per-frame compositing blend that mobile GPUs pay for.

(6) WebKit page-pinch fallback: `document.addEventListener('gesturestart', (e) => e.preventDefault())` — non-standard WebKit-only event, inert elsewhere, stops iOS Safari page zoom from stealing the two-finger gesture M2 needs.

(7) tests/view.test.ts (node env, no DOM — matches repo convention): dpr 1 passes through unchanged; 390×844 @ 3 clamps to 2; a 2560×1440 @ 2 clamps by area; dpr never returns < 1.
tasks.risks: Playwright's default deviceScaleFactor is 1, so `view.dpr === 1` in `scripts/sweep.mjs` and the art baselines are untouched — assert that explicitly in the harness (M8) because an accidental DPR change silently reshoots every baseline. Missing a single `canvas.width` call site produces a 2×-offset picking bug that only reproduces on a retina display; the grep must come back clean. `alpha:false` is only safe while both modes keep their full-canvas clear — a future partial-clear render path would show garbage.

tasks.title: Extract input intents, then add a Pointer-Events touch layer for battle mode
tasks.detail:
Two steps, and the first one is a pure refactor so the touch layer reuses the desktop state machine instead of forking it.

STEP 1 — lift the bodies of the existing canvas handlers into named functions in main.ts, called from the same listeners (no behavior change): `tapSelect(sx, sy, additive)` from the `if (!dragged)` block (main.ts:541-604), with the five `e.shiftKey` reads becoming the `additive` param; `beginBox(sx,sy)` / `updateBox(sx,sy)` / `commitBox(additive)` from 465-468, 480-492, 516-539; `beginOrderAnchor(sx,sy)` from 469-473; `commitOrder(sx, sy, { squadForce, floors })` from the whole window-mouseup-button-2 body (621-696) with `e.shiftKey`→`squadForce` and `e.altKey`→`floors`; `escapeLadder(): boolean` from the cancel branch (739-757); `stratTapSelect(sx,sy)` and `stratOrderMove(sx,sy)` from 503-513 and 610-616. Verify with `npm test` + `node scripts/demo.mjs` (it drives real clicks/keys) + `node scripts/sweep.mjs` before writing a line of touch code.

STEP 2 — `src/ui/touch.ts`. Pure, unit-testable half: `export const TAP_SLOP = 12; export const HOLD_MS = 420; export const TWO_TAP_MS = 260;` and `export function classify({ dt, dist, fingers, maxFingers }): 'tap'|'pan'|'pinch'|'hold'|'holdDrag'|'twoTap'`. DOM half: `bindTouch(canvas, handlers)` attaching `pointerdown/pointermove/pointerup/pointercancel` with `{passive:false}` and tracking pointers in a `Map<pointerId,{x0,y0,x,y,t0}>`. Two hard rules: ignore `e.pointerType === 'mouse'` outright (a touchscreen laptop keeps the exact desktop path), and attach one `touchstart` listener on the canvas with `{passive:false}` that calls `preventDefault()` — that is the reliable cross-engine way to suppress the synthesized `mousedown/mousemove/mouseup` that would otherwise re-enter the desktop handlers and double-fire every gesture.

Gesture → intent mapping (battle):
• 1 finger past TAP_SLOP before HOLD_MS → PAN. `cam.x -= dxCss / cam.scale; cam.y -= dyCss / cam.scale` per move (world point stays under the finger), then `cam.clampCenter(...)` from M5. If SELECT box-mode is armed (M3), the same drag calls `beginBox/updateBox/commitBox` instead — this is the box-select alternative: an explicit mode, because a drag has to mean pan by default on a map this big.
• 1 finger released under HOLD_MS and under TAP_SLOP → TAP = `tapSelect(x, y, addMode)`. The existing `targetMode` branches inside it already handle barrage/air/wheel/empfire/empsmoke placement with a single tap, no new code.
• 1 finger held ≥ HOLD_MS without moving → HOLD = the right-click equivalent. On the timer firing: call `beginOrderAnchor(x,y)` (sets `rmbDown`/`rmbAnchor`, which lights up the existing formation-drag preview at main.ts:922-931 and the armed-order danger dots for free), and write `mouse.x = x; mouse.y = y; mouse.onCanvas = true` so `pickAt`/tooltip/`cursor` (main.ts:914-916) resolve to the finger — that is the whole hover-emulation problem solved with three assignments and no frame-loop change. Draw a growing ring during the hold so the arm is legible. Movement after the hold is HOLDDRAG → the existing `len >= 2` formation branch (facing + width). On release: `commitOrder(x, y, { squadForce: addMode, floors: sim.map.storiesAt(Math.floor(wx), Math.floor(wy)) >= 2 })`, then clear `mouse.onCanvas`. `floors: true` reproduces Alt+right-click: the existing 633-642 branch pops `showFloorMenu` and the picked level becomes the order's `l`, so the multi-story feature needs no modifier.
• 2 fingers → PINCH: `cam.zoom(distNow / distPrev, midX, midY, view.w, view.h)` per move plus midpoint-delta pan; cancels any pending hold. This is the only zoom path on touch — there is no wheel event.
• 2-finger tap (both down and released inside TWO_TAP_MS, under TAP_SLOP) → `escapeLadder()` (targetMode → armedOrder → selectedTeam → selection). Deliberately does NOT fall through to opening the pause menu the way Esc does at main.ts:749-755 — a stray two-finger tap must never pause the battle; MENU is an explicit button in M3.
• `pointercancel`, or any pointer leaving the canvas, resets all gesture state and clears `mouse.onCanvas`.

tests/touch.test.ts covers `classify` only (node env, no DOM) — same split the repo already uses for `coach.ts` and `keymap.ts`.
tasks.risks: Double-firing (touch → synthesized mouse) is the main hazard. If any engine still double-fires after the `touchstart` preventDefault, add `let lastTouchAt = 0` in touch.ts and an early `if (performance.now() - lastTouchAt < 700) return;` at the top of the four mouse handlers — inert on a mouse-only device, so still byte-identical in practice. HOLD_MS 420 / TAP_SLOP 12 need tuning on real hardware: too tight and a shaky finger pans instead of ordering, too loose and ordering feels laggy. The Step-1 refactor touches the highest-traffic code in the repo — land it as its own commit with the sweep + demo harnesses green so any regression is bisectable.

tasks.title: Responsive battle HUD: bottom-sheet roster, order/action bar, docked tooltip
tasks.detail:
New `src/ui/device.ts`: `export const MOBILE = typeof matchMedia === 'function' && matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)').matches && Math.min(innerWidth, innerHeight) <= 820;` and at boot `document.documentElement.classList.toggle('mobile', MOBILE)`. Every rule below is scoped `html.mobile …`, so no existing desktop selector changes — byte-identical by construction, and the claim is mechanically checkable (M8).

(1) `#touchbar` — the order-kind picker replacing 1-9 / Shift+1-8. Built in the `Hud` constructor only when MOBILE, appended to `hud.root`, `pointer-events:auto`, two rows. Row 1: the 8 order chips rendered from the same `ORDER_KINDS` + `canArm(k, target)` + `st.armedOrder === k ? ' armed'` logic as `orderBar()` (hud.ts:438-450) and carrying the same `data-order` attribute, so arming flows through the existing `cb.armOrder` delegation untouched. Row 2: SELECT (box-mode toggle for M2), ADD (sticky shift-equivalent for multi-select and force-squad-order), ALL (select every `infantrySquads(sim)` id — the order-burst amortization decision of 2026-07-24 already made select-all-then-order affordable), CANCEL (`escapeLadder`), ☄ Barrage, ✈ Airstrike, ⏸, ☰ Menu. Add `toggleBoxMode`, `toggleAddMode`, `selectAll`, `cancel`, `openMenu` to `HudCallbacks` and wire them in main.ts's `new Hud({...})`. Render inside the existing sig-gated `update()`. NOTE: the click delegation is currently bound to `#squads` (hud.ts:134) — bind a second listener on `#touchbar` or move delegation to `hud.root`.
CSS: `html.mobile #touchbar{position:fixed;left:0;right:0;bottom:0;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:4px;padding:6px 6px calc(6px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom));background:rgba(var(--ink-rgb),0.92);border-top:1px solid var(--border);backdrop-filter:var(--glass-blur);pointer-events:auto}`; `html.mobile #touchbar>div{display:flex;gap:4px;overflow-x:auto;scrollbar-width:none;touch-action:pan-x}`; `html.mobile .ord, html.mobile #touchbar .hbtn{min-height:44px;min-width:44px;font-size:var(--fs-md)}` (today `.ord` is ~28×18px at `font-size:10px;padding:3px 7px` — roughly a third of the minimum touch target).

(2) Roster → bottom sheet, so the 266px left panel stops eating a phone screen: `html.mobile #squads{left:0;right:0;width:auto;top:auto;bottom:var(--touchbar-h,104px);max-height:38dvh;padding:0 6px;touch-action:pan-y;transform:translateY(calc(100% - 52px));transition:transform .18s ease}` plus `html.mobile #squads.open{transform:none}`, with a 44px `#squads-handle` row toggling `.open`. Collapsed = card heads only (`html.mobile #squads:not(.open) .srow, … .orderbar, … .bars-key{display:none}`), which turns 18 squads + weapons teams into a scannable strip; expanded = today's full cards. Selecting a squad from the world auto-collapses; the existing `scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'})` (hud.ts:371) keeps working.

(3) Kill the desktop-only chrome on mobile: `html.mobile #hint{display:none}` (its two `white-space:nowrap` keyboard-legend spans wrap to ~8 lines at 390px, and worse, they feed `viewportInset` a huge bottom inset — see M5; `display:none` yields a zero-area rect, which the existing `r.width > 0` guard at main.ts:287-290 already drops). `html.mobile #banner{font-size:22px;letter-spacing:4px}` (34px + 8px letter-spacing overflows 390px). `html.mobile #obj-strip .obj-center{display:none}`. `html.mobile #modeline{top:auto;bottom:calc(112px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom));left:8px;right:8px;transform:none;text-align:center}`.

(4) Tooltip has no hover to hang on: `html.mobile #tip{position:fixed;left:6px;right:6px;bottom:calc(112px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom));top:auto!important;width:auto;max-height:34dvh;overflow-y:auto;touch-action:pan-y}` and skip the mouse-follow positioning block (tooltip.ts:194-202) when MOBILE. Content is driven by the tap/hold probe point M2 writes into `mouse.x/y` — the full aim-breakdown / shot-solution card the legibility pillar depends on stays reachable on a phone.

(5) Order-affordance tips are hover-only today (`mouseover`/`mouseout`/`mouseleave`, hud.ts:152-160): on mobile trigger `showAffordance` from a long-press on an order chip, and clamp its position (`left: Math.min(r.left, innerWidth - 198)`) — it currently anchors to `r.left` with a fixed 190px width and will hang off a narrow screen.

(6) Canvas-side chrome that assumes width: `EventPings.draw` puts a 190px feed at `cw - 202` (overlays.ts:376, 417) → `const rw = Math.min(ROW_W, cw - 24)` and cap visible rows to 3 when `cw < 500`. And the coach/idle copy names keys (main.ts:127, 148; hud.ts:236-248) — swap in touch wording under MOBILE.
tasks.risks: `dvh` and `env()` need Safari 15.4+ / Chrome 108+; ship `vh` and `0px` fallbacks first in each declaration. Two stacked fixed bottom layers (sheet + bar) must agree on height: publish it as `--touchbar-h` set from JS after first layout and feed the same number into `viewportInset` (M5), or the sheet and bar overlap. Eight 44px chips do not fit 390px — they must scroll horizontally; shrinking the font to fit re-creates the untappable target this task exists to fix.

tasks.title: Strategic mode: sector camera, touch gestures, and DOM clock controls
tasks.detail:
(1) The blocker, first: strategic mode hides `hud.root` (main.ts:838) and exposes pause/speed only as Space and Digit1/2/3 (main.ts:733-763), while boot state is `stratPaused = true` (main.ts:82). On touch the campaign clock can never be started — the game is unplayable from the first screen, ahead of every other item in this plan. Add a control cluster to `#st-progress` (rendered in strat-hud.ts:174-180): `▶/⏸` plus `1× / 10× / 60×` buttons, wired through new StratHud callbacks to `stratPaused` and `speedIdx`, with `.active` on the current speed. Render them on desktop too — the mouse currently has no strategic pause affordance either, and the keyboard paths stay untouched.

(2) Give `StrategicView` a camera. Today `layout()` (strategic.ts:77-80) is fit-only: on a 390×844 phone the 40×25 sector solves to `min(390/40, (844-58)/25)` = 9px cells, and a 9px chit with a letter drawn in it (strategic.ts:114-148) is neither readable nor tappable. Add fields `zoomMul = 1; panX = 0; panY = 0;` and make `layout()` return `size = Math.max(4, Math.floor(fitSize * zoomMul))`, `ox = Math.floor((canvasW - size*w)/2) + panX`, `oy = HEADER_H + panY`, with a `clampPan()` that keeps the grid from being flung past the viewport centre. `cellAtScreen` already derives from `layout()`, so hit-testing follows for free. Defaults `zoomMul = 1, panX = panY = 0` reproduce today's pixels exactly.

(3) `fitCells(canvasW, canvasH, minCellPx = 26)`: on mobile boot set `zoomMul = Math.max(1, minCellPx / fitSize)` and pan to centre the blue chits' bounding box. 26px is the floor for a tap target on a chit.

(4) Touch, via M2's `bindTouch` with a strategic handler set: 1-finger drag → pan (`panX += dx; panY += dy; clampPan()`); pinch → `zoomMul *= factor` clamped `[1, 4]` about the midpoint; tap → `stratTapSelect(x,y)`; hold → `stratOrderMove(x,y)` (the right-click equivalent, preserving the river-refusal flash at main.ts:613-614); two-finger tap → deselect (`selectedChit = -1`).

(5) Narrow-viewport canvas chrome: skip `drawLegend` (a 216×101px box, strategic.ts:452) and `drawHintBar` (strategic.ts:438 — `HINT_TEXT` is a pure keyboard legend) when `canvasW < 700`; skip `drawSelectedPanel` (220px, strategic.ts:514) when MOBILE, since `#st-chit-panel` already shows a strict superset of the same data. Restyle the DOM panels as sheets: `html.mobile #st-chit-panel{left:0;right:0;bottom:0;width:auto;max-height:40dvh;border-radius:0}`; `html.mobile #st-roster{left:0;right:0;width:auto;bottom:auto;top:calc(84px + env(safe-area-inset-top))}` (already collapsed by default — keep it that way); `html.mobile .st-wp-cancel{width:32px;height:32px;font-size:18px}` (18×18px today, a coin-flip tap that deletes a march order).

(6) Test the pure part in tests/strategic.test.ts: a tap at the centre of cell (x,y) round-trips through `layout()`/`cellAtScreen` under non-default `zoomMul`/pan; and `zoomMul === 1 && panX === panY === 0` reproduces the current `size/ox/oy` numbers exactly.
tasks.risks: `layout()` is the single source of truth for both drawing and hit-testing, so a pan/zoom sign error silently mis-targets march orders — the round-trip test is the guard. The strategic control cluster changes a shared (non-mobile-gated) render path in strat-hud.ts, so it will shift `#st-progress` layout on desktop screenshots; that is a deliberate desktop improvement, not an accident, and should be called out rather than hidden behind `html.mobile`.

tasks.title: Boot framing and camera limits under a small viewport
tasks.detail:
The 2026-07-24 clear-viewport boot-framing decision is correct on desktop and actively harmful on a phone, because it trusts every measured inset.

(1) `viewportInset()` (main.ts:282-299) returns `left = squads.right`. Once `#squads` is a full-width bottom sheet (M3), that is ≈`innerWidth` → `vw = Math.max(1, cw - inset.left) = 1` → `fit ≈ 0` → the zoomed branch computes `scale = Math.min(48, Math.max(2, 1/120)) = 2` px/m: the player opens a battle at 2px/m looking at nothing. Fix with an overlay cap, extracted pure for testing: `export function capInset(v: number, extent: number, frac = 0.35): number { return v > extent * frac ? 0 : v; }` applied to left, top and bottom. The rationale is the decision log's own logic taken one step further — chrome that eats more than a third of an axis is a drawer, not a border, and insetting against it is worse than ignoring it.

(2) Feed the real mobile chrome in: `bottom = capInset(Math.max(hintInset, touchbarInset), ch)`, reading `#touchbar`'s rect (M3). `#hint` is `display:none` on mobile, so the existing `r.width > 0 && r.height > 0` guard already drops it — the same guard that fixed the collapsed-strategic-DOM bug.

(3) Framing distance: `scale = Math.min(48, Math.max(2, vw / 120))` (main.ts:341) encodes a desktop viewing distance. Add `const FRAME_M = MOBILE ? 70 : 120`. On a ~374px clear region, 120m across is 3.1 px/m — below the 5 px/m dot-LOD threshold the art direction sets, i.e. the player's opening shot of their own company is a field of dots; 70m lands at ~5.3 px/m and reads as soldiers.

(4) `WHOLE_MAP_PX_M = 2.5` (main.ts:314) stays as-is. On a phone a 320×240 map fits at ~1.2 px/m, so the whole-map branch is unreachable — which is the right answer; the zoomed branch with FRAME_M 70 is the better phone opening, and the threshold needs no mobile variant.

(5) `src/render/camera.ts`: replace the inline clamps in `zoom()` (camera.ts:21) with `minScale = 2; maxScale = 48;` fields — defaults preserve desktop byte-for-byte — so mobile can set `cam.minScale = Math.min(2, fitScale)` (pinching out to see the whole 320m map needs ~1.2 px/m, which the hard 2 forbids today) and `cam.maxScale = 32` (M6's memory cap). Add `clampCenter(mapW, mapH, viewW, viewH)` called ONLY from M2's touch pan/pinch path; WASD pan (main.ts:827-837) stays unclamped so desktop behavior is untouched.

(6) `needsBootFrame` (main.ts:973-979) already re-frames on the first battle frame after the HUD lays out, which is exactly what mobile needs — but `#touchbar` and the roster sheet must exist by then, so build them in the `Hud` constructor (M3), never lazily on first selection.

(7) tests/framing.test.ts: `capInset` boundaries (just under / just over `frac`), and a `bootCamera` call with a stubbed inset set mimicking the phone sheet — assert `scale > 3` px/m and the blue centroid inside the clear rect, the same two properties the original framing fix was measured against.
tasks.risks: `capInset`'s 0.35 threshold is a judgement call: at a 1024px tablet width the 266px roster is 26% and still insets correctly, but a narrow desktop window (760px) crosses the line and would stop insetting — verify against the desktop widths that matter before landing, or key the cap on MOBILE only. Relaxing `minScale` lets a mobile player zoom out past the useful LOD range; pair it with `clampCenter` so the map cannot be flung off-screen at 1.2 px/m.

tasks.title: Mobile GPU and memory budget: cache caps, bake budget, sim catch-up guard
tasks.detail:
M1 caps the backing store (dpr ≤ 2, ≤ 2.6 Mpx). What remains are the caches and the first-frame bake, which are what actually kill a mobile Safari tab.

(1) `PIXEL_BUDGET = 24_000_000` (terrain.ts:12) is ~96MB of RGBA chunk canvases, on top of the `dudes.ts` sprite cache and the decal atlas — over iOS Safari's practical canvas-memory tolerance. Set `MOBILE ? 6_000_000 : 24_000_000`.

(2) Drop the top band on mobile: `BANDS = MOBILE ? [4,8,16,32] : [4,8,16,32,48]` (terrain.ts:11), so the worst-case chunk canvas is `(16+2)*32 = 576²` = 331k px instead of 746k. Pairs with `cam.maxScale = 32` from M5, so nothing is ever upscaled.

(3) The first-frame hitch: `TerrainLayer.draw` (terrain.ts:581-598) calls `this.chunk(cx, cy, band)` inside the visible-chunk loop with no budget. At a mobile boot zoom a 320×240 map is 20×15 = 300 synchronous bakes in one frame, each running the hedge-capsule, tree, water-bank and hillshade passes — seconds of frozen white screen. Add a mobile-only budget: `let baked = 0; const BAKE_BUDGET = 12;` per `draw()`; when spent, fill the chunk's rect with the flat terrain base colour and record it in a `pending` set so later frames finish it. Gate on MOBILE — the art gate screenshots frame 1, so a desktop budget would change baselines.

(4) `dudes.ts` (BANDS `[6,12,24,48]`, dudes.ts:17-19): cap `bandFor` at 24 on mobile. Band 48 bakes ~90² canvases per (pose × frame × weapon × side) on demand, and with `maxScale = 32` the phone never displays it.

(5) `MAX_VOICES = 28` (audio.ts:41) → 12 on mobile: each voice is a BufferSource plus two BiquadFilters, and mobile WebAudio distorts and drops out well below 28 concurrent. Audio unlock itself already works on touch (`window.addEventListener('pointerdown', unlockAudio)`, main.ts:100) — no change needed there, which is worth stating so nobody 'fixes' it.

(6) Sim catch-up death spiral: `frame()` caps `dtReal` at 250ms (main.ts:825) and then runs `while (acc >= DT_MS)` (888-893) — up to 7 sim steps in a single frame. On a phone that already missed its budget, that guarantees it misses the next one worse. On mobile cap it at 3 steps and drop the remainder (`acc = 0`): let the sim run slow rather than lock the UI. Mobile-gated, so desktop determinism and the perf tests are untouched.

(7) Verify, don't assume: Playwright/`mcp__chrome-devtools__emulate` at 390×844 with 4× CPU throttling — target ≥ 24fps at boot framing with 247 soldiers, and total heap + canvas memory under ~150MB via a heap snapshot. Record the numbers the way the 2026-07-24 order-burst entry records its 3 isolated runs.
tasks.risks: MOBILE gating creates a second render path that desktop CI never exercises — the bake fallback in particular is visible as flat-colour squares if BAKE_BUDGET is too low; keep it ≥ 8/frame and confirm the fill-in completes within ~3 frames. Dropping band 48 and lowering the pixel budget changes mobile appearance only, but a too-small budget causes cache thrash (re-baking the same chunks every pan) that is slower than the memory it saves — measure evictions, don't guess the constant.

tasks.title: PWA/meta niceties, portrait guidance banner, touch coachmarks
tasks.detail:
(1) index.html: `theme-color`, `apple-mobile-web-app-capable=yes`, `apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style=black-translucent` (the pair that makes `viewport-fit=cover` plus the `env(safe-area-inset-*)` padding from M3 actually pay off), and `<link rel="manifest" href="./manifest.webmanifest">` — RELATIVE, matching the 2026-07-24 `base: './'` deploy decision; an absolute `/manifest.webmanifest` 404s on every subpath host that decision exists to support.

(2) `public/manifest.webmanifest` (Vite copies `public/` verbatim): `name`, `short_name`, `display: "standalone"`, `orientation: "landscape"`, `background_color` and `theme_color` `"#1a1d1a"` (matching the existing body background), and one 512px icon. No service worker — offline play is not a goal for a portfolio piece, and a stale SW cache on a personal site is a self-inflicted support burden.

(3) Portrait guidance: a `#rotate` div created next to `#debrief` in main.ts, shown by CSS alone so there is no resize plumbing to get wrong — `#rotate{display:none}` and `@media (orientation:portrait){html.mobile #rotate:not(.dismissed){display:flex;position:fixed;inset:0;z-index:30;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;justify-content:center;background:#0d0f0b;…}}`. Copy names the reason rather than scolding: 'The battlefield is 320m wide — rotate to landscape', plus a 'Play in portrait anyway' button that adds `.dismissed`. `orientation: "landscape"` in the manifest covers installed mode.

(4) First-touch coachmarks through the existing `coach` (src/ui/coach.ts, already localStorage-gated with a dismiss ✕): add `touch-basics` — 'Drag to pan · pinch to zoom · press and hold to give an order' — on the first battle frame under MOBILE, and `touch-order` on the first squad selection, replacing the keyboard copy currently passed at main.ts:127 and 148. Coach's horizontal clamp already handles narrow viewports (coach.ts:53-59), but `.coach{max-width:280px}` should become `max-width:min(280px, calc(100vw - 24px))`.

(5) One honesty fix while in the HUD copy: the hint at hud.ts:113/257 advertises 'shift+right-click waypoint', but `sim.queueMove` — the only waypoint-queue entry point — has zero production callers (only tests/sim.test.ts and tests/assault.test.ts), and main.ts's shift path calls `orderSquad`, which CLEARS `squadWaypoints` (sim.ts:1347). The touch order bar must not replicate a feature the live game cannot reach: either wire `queueMove` to a real input (an ADD-mode hold, say) or drop the claim from both hint strings and the `squadWaypoints` route overlay.
tasks.risks: A manifest with `display:standalone` invites installation, and an installed shell that hides the browser UI makes any layout bug unescapable — verify the safe-area padding in standalone mode on a notched device before shipping the manifest. The waypoint cleanup is a behavior decision, not a mobile task: fixing the hint text is safe, wiring `queueMove` live is a gameplay change that needs its own review.

tasks.title: Mobile verification harness and desktop-regression proof
tasks.detail:
'Keep desktop byte-identical' is a falsifiable claim, so make it mechanically checkable instead of asserted.

(1) `scripts/lib/stage.mjs`: extend `launch()` to `launch({ device } = {})` with an opt-in phone profile — `{ viewport: {width:390,height:844}, deviceScaleFactor: 3, isMobile: true, hasTouch: true }` — while the default stays `1280×800` at deviceScaleFactor 1, so `sweep.mjs`, `demo.mjs`, `vfx.mjs` and `shot.mjs` baselines are unaffected. Note `burst()` reads `canvas.width` for its ROI (stage.mjs), which stays self-consistent under any DPR because probe and source share it.

(2) Add a preflight assert to `sweep.mjs`: `view.dpr === 1` and `document.documentElement.classList.contains('mobile') === false`. An accidental DPR or MOBILE flip silently reshoots every art baseline, and a reshot baseline is an invisible regression.

(3) `scripts/mobile.mjs`: portrait + landscape phone captures of (a) strategic boot with the new clock controls, (b) a staged battle at boot framing (assert the blue centroid is inside the clear region — the same property the 2026-07-24 framing entry measured), (c) roster sheet open, (d) mid-hold order gesture, driven with `page.touchscreen.tap` and dispatched pointer sequences. Fail the run on any console error and on `document.documentElement.scrollWidth > innerWidth` — a horizontal-overflow guard the fixed layout must never trip.

(4) `mobile.mjs --desktop-regression` re-runs `sweep.mjs` at the desktop profile and diffs against the pre-change baselines; a non-zero diff means a mobile rule leaked out of an `html.mobile` selector. This is the actual proof of the additive claim.

(5) Extend the `__game` automation seam (main.ts:796-818) with `view`, `MOBILE`, and the gesture `classify` function so the harness can assert gesture classification without synthesising timing-sensitive touch sequences.

(6) Log the decision in `docs/decisions/INDEX.md` under UI: the touch grammar (1-finger drag pan / pinch zoom / tap select / press-and-hold order / hold-drag formation / two-finger tap cancel / explicit SELECT box-mode), the persistent armed-order bar chosen over a context radial (the armed-order state machine and its danger-preview already exist — a radial would fork it and add new hit-testing for no new capability), and the rejected alternatives (two-finger tap opening the pause menu; a global `touch-action:none`; a service worker).
tasks.risks: Synthetic touch sequences are timing-sensitive and flaky in headless Chrome — assert on resulting game state (`__game.cam`, `selectedSquads`, order state) rather than on screenshots wherever possible, and keep the gesture-classifier assertions in the pure vitest layer. The desktop-regression diff is only meaningful if the baselines were captured before the mobile work starts; capture them in the first commit of the effort, not the last.

units.summary: The unit art is a competent parametric skeleton that has never been pushed past band-12 fidelity: `src/render/dudes.ts` draws every soldier from ~6 primitives (torso ellipse, two `cap()` limbs, helmet dome, one gun line whose only variation is a 3-way `gunClass` length switch), and `src/render/vehicles.ts` draws each kind from flat rects with a single track-link stroke and no per-instance or per-motion state. At bands 24/48 the bake budget is enormous and unspent: 1 body unit = 32.4 px (band 24) / 64.8 px (band 48), so a helmet is 11-23 px across and a 0.03-unit hairline is 1-2 px — there is room for webbing, pouch rows, helmet netting, weld seams and hatch detail that simply is not drawn. The most conspicuous art-direction violation is lighting: `contactShadow()` and `hullShadow()` are baked *inside* the rotating sprite, so the "one sun" (`src/render/light.ts`, NW, shadows SE) is destroyed at draw time — a tank facing east and one facing west throw shadows in opposite directions, and every soldier's helmet highlight points wherever he happens to face. Nothing else is wrong architecturally: the bake/band framework, the `haloMult()` zoom-attenuated rim, and the pure `drawImage`+transform frame loop are all sound and every task below stays inside them. Two hazards must be respected: the sprite cache is unbounded and keyed on 5 dimensions already (band-48 dude canvas = 173²×4 B ≈ 117 KB, so a realistic live set of 2 sides × 6 weapons × 24 pose-frames ≈ 34 MB at that band), and the perf floor is 247 soldiers ≥ 100 fps against a measured 8.8 ms/frame baseline, which allows roughly one extra small `drawImage` per soldier and no more.

tasks.title: Bake scaffolding: detail tiers, hairline clamp, bounded sprite cache, band prewarm, vehicle art-gate crop
tasks.detail:
Foundation every other task imports; land it first, alone, so the guardrails exist before the detail lands.

1) **Detail tiers.** Export from dudes.ts: `export function tier(band: number): 0|1|2|3 { return band >= 48 ? 3 : band >= 24 ? 2 : band >= 12 ? 1 : 0; }` and the same for vehicles.ts (or import). Contract: tier 0 = silhouette + team rim ONLY (band 6; today's straps/gear/pack blocks are sub-pixel mush there — delete them at tier 0, it is both cleaner and faster); tier 1 = today's look; tier 2 = webbing/pouches/per-weapon geometry/role marks/panel lines; tier 3 = helmet netting, pack lacing, bolt rows, weathering, fillText markings. Every new draw call in U3-U8 is gated `if (t >= 2)` / `if (t >= 3)`.

2) **Hairline clamp.** Bake space differs per module: dudes' ctx is `scale(band*DUDE_SCALE)` so one device pixel = `1/(band*1.35)` body units (0.0154 at band 48, 0.0309 at 24, 0.0617 at 12); vehicles' ctx is `scale(band)` so one pixel = `1/band` metres. Add `const hair = (band: number) => 1 / (band * DUDE_SCALE)` (dudes) / `1 / band` (vehicles) and route every new `lineWidth`/dot radius through `Math.max(w, hair(band))`. Without this, the panel lines and pouch ticks specced below vanish at band 24 and alias at band 12.

3) **Bounded cache.** Replace the bare `Map` in both modules with insertion-order LRU: on hit `cache.delete(key); cache.set(key, c)`; after insert, while `bytes > BUDGET` evict `cache.keys().next().value`. Track `bytes += c.width*c.height*4`. `DUDE_BUDGET = 48<<20`, `VEHICLE_BUDGET = 24<<20`. Expose `spriteCacheStats()` returning `{entries, bytes}` for the perf gate. This is load-bearing: U4 adds a role/veterancy `variant` dimension and U6 adds `crawl`×4 + `dead`×3, which multiply the existing side×weapon×pose×frame×band keyspace.

4) **Key hygiene.** `surrendered` and `dragged` ignore the weapon entirely (`surrendered()` hardcodes `'garand'`), yet bake one canvas per weapon. In `getSprite`, normalise: `const wk = (pose === 'surrendered' || pose === 'dragged') ? 'garand' : weapon;` and key on `wk`. Collapse any tier-gated dimension below its tier in the key builder, never at the draw site — e.g. `const v = tier(band) >= 2 ? variant : 0` before the key string is built, so far bands cannot mint extra entries.

5) **Prewarm.** Baking is lazy inside the frame, so a zoom that crosses a band boundary hitches harder once bakes get expensive. In renderer.ts, when `bandFor(cam.scale)` changes, queue a `requestIdleCallback` that bakes {idle, aim, walk 0..5} for each (side, weapon) actually present in `sim.soldiers` at the new band, and every present (kind, side) vehicle sprite. Bail out if the band changes again.

6) **Art-gate coverage.** `scripts/lib/stage.mjs` `deriveTargets()` has no vehicle scene, so U5/U7 would ship unregressed — the exact blind spot that let German kits go untested until the `enemy` crop was added. Add `vehicles: { ...squadCentroid('blue'), scale: 48 }` plus a stage helper that places one of each kind (`sim.addVehicle('blue','sherman',...)`, panzer4, stug3, m3_halftrack, sdkfz251) in a row 6 m apart on four different headings (0, π/2, π, 3π/4 — heading spread is what exposes the rotating-shadow bug fixed in U2), and a `soldiers48` crop at `scale: 48`. Register both in sweep.mjs's crop list.

Verify: `npm run check`, `npm test`, `node scripts/shot.mjs --preset units`, `node scripts/sweep.mjs` contact sheet unchanged except the two new crops (tier 0/1 output must be byte-similar — this task changes no tier-1 art except deleting tier-0 sub-pixel gear).
tasks.risks: Tier 0 gear deletion is a real (if tiny) visual change at band 6 — confirm on the farlod/sweep crops that nothing reads worse. LRU eviction can thrash if BUDGET is set too low for a wide weapon mix at band 48; measure `spriteCacheStats()` at the units crop and raise the budget rather than letting per-frame re-bakes into the frame loop.

tasks.title: One sun on units: world-aligned cast shadows for soldiers, vehicles and wrecks, plus a rotation-correct helmet glint
tasks.detail:
The single biggest fidelity defect and the one explicit compromise in the current code (`contactShadow()` comment: "an ambient blob is the documented tradeoff"). It is fixable without leaving the bake framework, because a shadow's *silhouette* can be baked in body space while its *direction* is applied by the draw-time matrix.

**Length convention — match what already exists.** roofs.ts uses `shadowOffset(0.71 * stories)` for a 3 m story and `shadowOffset(1.1 * stories)` for the soft layer; terrain hedges use `shadowOffset(0.4)` on a ~2 m mass. So the house convention is a heavily foreshortened ≈0.24×height core / ≈0.37×height soft, NOT the geometric 1.19×height that 40° elevation implies. Follow it: standing soldier (1.75 m) → core 0.42 m, soft 0.62 m; prone/dead → core 0.12 m; vehicle hull (2.4 m) → core 0.58 m, soft 0.90 m; turret roof (2.9 m) → 0.70 m. Note that today's `hullShadow` uses `shadowOffset(long*0.22)` = 1.28 m for a Sherman — double the convention *and* rotating with the hull. Both wrong, both fixed here.

**Silhouette bakes.** `getShadowSprite(pose, frame, gunClass, band)` in dudes.ts and `getVehicleShadow(kind, state, band)` in vehicles.ts. Bake at `SHADOW_BAKE_BAND = Math.min(24, band)` — the sprite is a soft blob, so a 2× bilinear upscale at band 48 *is* the feathering (44-87 px canvases, ~8-30 KB each; 24 pose-frames × 3 gun classes ≈ 0.6 MB total, and shadows carry no side/weapon/variant dimension so the whole army shares a handful of textures, which also keeps the compositor happy). Implementation: run the existing `drawDude`/`drawSherman`-family code paths with a monochrome kit where every colour is `rgba(20,16,10,1)`, skipping the team rim, straps, gear, markings and the baked contact ellipse. Do NOT use `ctx.filter = 'blur()'`; the upscale is the softener and filter support is an unnecessary bet.

**Draw pass.** One new `drawUnitShadows(ctx, cam, ...)` called in `renderer.draw()` immediately after `this.terrain.drawStairs(...)` (renderer.ts:139) and before the dead-vehicle pass at :145 — after decals so shadows fall on craters, before every unit so no shadow lands on top of a body. Skip entirely when `cam.scale < 10` (sub-pixel) or `s.level > 0` (upper-floor men don't shadow the street). Respect the same `vis(s)`/`visV(v)` FoW gates and the `dim()` floor-focus alpha. Per unit:
```
const A = Math.atan2(SUN.dy, SUN.dx);      // module const, sun azimuth in screen space
ctx.save(); ctx.translate(x, y);
ctx.rotate(A); ctx.translate(off * cam.scale, 0); ctx.scale(stretch, 1); ctx.rotate(-A);
ctx.rotate(facing);
ctx.globalAlpha = SHADOW_SOFT_ALPHA;       // 0.14, one soft layer only
ctx.drawImage(shadowSpr, -pad/2, -pad/2, pad, pad);
ctx.restore();
```
with `off` = the metre value above, `stretch` = 1.18 standing / 1.05 prone-dead / 1.30 vehicles (elongation along the sun axis only). If profiling shows the 3-rotate chain matters, hand-multiply `R(A)·T(off,0)·S(stretch,1)·R(-A)·R(facing)` into a single `ctx.transform(a,b,c,d,e,f)` — but measure first.

**Retire the baked blobs.** In dudes.ts shrink `contactShadow` to a pure contact AO: single ellipse `0.18 × 0.13` units at `rgba(20,16,10, AO_ALPHA*0.5)`, delete the `elongated` long-ellipse branch (the cast pass owns elongation now). In vehicles.ts delete `hullShadow` from the bake entirely and add a tight `rgba(14,13,10, AO_ALPHA*0.6)` inset ring hugging the hull outline instead.

**Turret drop shadow (vehicles only, tier ≥ 2).** The turret sits ~1 m above the deck and does not traverse in sim, but the sun does not rotate with the hull — so bake ONE shared soft ellipse sprite (`rgba(10,9,7,1)` radial → transparent, 32 px) and draw it unrotated at the turret's world position offset down-sun: `tx = v.x + (tcx*cos f - tcy*sin f) + SUN.dx*0.70`, same for y, radius ≈ turret r × 1.05. Export the turret centre per kind from vehicles.ts (`turretCenter(kind): [number, number]`, e.g. sherman `[-0.15, 0]`, panzer4 `[-0.1, 0]`, stug3 `null`). This is the detail that makes a turret read as sitting *on* the hull rather than painted onto it.

**Helmet glint (soldiers, cam.scale ≥ 16).** The baked `rgba(255,255,255,0.14)` blob inside `helmet()` points wherever the man faces — delete it at tier ≥ 2 (keep at tier ≤ 1). Replace with one shared 32×32 baked sprite: white `0.18`→transparent radial centred at 35% toward NW, plus a `rgba(0,0,0,0.10)` crescent on the SE limb. Draw it *unrotated* (no save/restore needed beyond fillStyle-free `drawImage`) at the head's world position, using a `HEAD_OFFSET: Record<Pose, [number, number]>` table in body units read straight off the existing `helmet(g, k, x, y)` call sites (idle/aim/surrendered `[0.04, 0]`, walk `[0.04, -bob]`→use `[0.04, 0]`, kneel `[0.06, 0]`, prone/downed/dead `[0.42, 0]`, drag `[0.10, 0]`, aid `[0.13, 0]`, dragged `[0.32, 0]`, melee `[0.05, 0]`), rotated by facing: `hx*cos f - hy*sin f` scaled by `DUDE_SCALE*cam.scale`. Size ≈ `0.42 * DUDE_SCALE * cam.scale` px. Two trig calls and one small textured quad per soldier — the cheapest possible way to put a consistent NW light on 247 heads.

Verify: the new `vehicles` crop with four headings must show all four shadows pointing SE and matching the direction of the nearest building shadow; `--preset units` at scale 48 shows every helmet lit from the same side. Perf gate is mandatory here: 247 soldiers × (1 shadow quad + 1 glint quad) against the 8.8 ms/114 fps baseline — measure with `scripts/demo.mjs`/`survey.mjs`, and if it exceeds ~1.5 ms drop the glint to `cam.scale >= 24` before touching anything else.
tasks.risks: This is the one task that adds per-soldier frame-loop work (2 extra drawImage). At 247 units the budget is tight — if the measurement misses ≥100 fps, the fallbacks in priority order are: glint at scale ≥ 24 only, shadow pass at scale ≥ 14 only, then hand-multiplied single ctx.transform. Second risk: 0.42 m soldier shadows at 247 units may read as visual clutter in a dense village fight — tune `off`/alpha on the village and units crops together, and treat the roofs convention as the ceiling, not a floor.

tasks.title: Per-WeaponKey silhouette table (M1 vs MG42 vs K98 readable at a glance)
tasks.detail:
Highest fidelity-per-byte in the whole plan, and zero cache cost: `weapon` is already a cache key, so nothing multiplies. Today `gun()` collapses 17 `WeaponKey`s into three lengths (`rifle 1.05 / smg 0.62 / mg 1.25`) — a Kar98k, a BAR, a bazooka and an 8 cm mortar are the same picture.

Replace the `w === 'rifle' ? ... :` chain with a table `const GUNS: Record<WeaponKey, GunShape>` where `GunShape = { len, back, barrelW, stock: 'wood'|'folding'|'none', mag?: [x, y, w, h, orient], bipod?: number, scope?: number, drum?: number, jacket?: number, tube?: number, muzzle?: 'brake'|'cone'|'none' }`, and a `gun()` that consumes it in draw order: stock → receiver → barrel → jacket ticks → magazine → bipod → scope → muzzle device. All lengths in body units (1 unit ≈ 1.35 m, so a 1.1 m Garand ≈ 0.82 units — the current 1.05 is already stylised long; keep the existing values as the baseline so silhouette scale does not shift, and differentiate by *shape*).

Per-key specifics (tier ≥ 2 for the sub-features, tier ≥ 3 for jacket/bolt ticks):
- `garand` len 1.05, wood stock `#5d4126`, thin op-rod tick along the underside, no mag box.
- `carbine` len 0.82, slimmer barrel (0.05), short 0.12 mag box below the receiver.
- `springfield` / `kar98k_scoped` len 1.15, `scope: 0.22` — a 0.2×0.07 block riding above the receiver with two ring ticks. This is the sniper read.
- `kar98k` len 1.02, straight bolt tick perpendicular at 0.15 behind the receiver, wood stock to the muzzle band.
- `bar` len 1.12, `bipod: 0.16` at the muzzle, 0.16 mag box below, thicker barrel 0.075.
- `thompson` len 0.66, `drum: 0.1` (or a 0.2 stick mag) plus a foregrip tick under the barrel; `mp40` len 0.62, `stock: 'folding'` (a thin 0.18 wire rectangle behind the receiver) and a *vertical* 0.22 mag hanging straight down — the two SMGs must not be the same shape.
- `m1919` len 1.2, thin barrel + `jacket: 5` perforation ticks, ammo-can rect 0.28×0.18 at the loader side, belt curve from the feed to the can; `mg42` len 1.32, fatter perforated jacket (7 ticks), `bipod: 0.2`, drum ring 0.11 on the left, a distinctly bulkier muzzle booster. The MG42/M1919 contrast is the highest-value pair in the game.
- `bazooka`/`schreck`: `tube: 1.4`/`1.5` — a constant-diameter 0.09 tube with NO stock taper, a 0.2×0.16 blast shield (schreck only) at the front third and a shoulder rest tick; drawn riding the shoulder line rather than in both hands (offset `gy` by -0.06).
- `panzerfaust`: 0.75 tube plus a 0.16-diameter warhead bulb at the muzzle. Unmistakable.
- `mortar60`/`mortar81`: on a soldier these are *carried*, not fired — draw a 0.9/1.1 tube slung diagonally across the back (`angle = 2.45`, same as the slung-weapon convention in `drag()`), plus a baseplate disc for `mortar81`. Firing mortars are emplacements (U8).
- `at57_gun`/`pak40_gun`: crew-served; the man carries a carbine-shaped stand-in (len 0.8, no mag) — these keys only reach a soldier sprite via crew loadouts.

Also make the two-handed grip follow the shape: the existing `fore = gunClass(w) === 'smg' ? 0.24 : 0.38` becomes `GUNS[w].fore` so a bazooka's support hand sits at 0.5 and an MP40's at 0.22 — hand placement is half of what makes a weapon read. Keep `WEAPONS[w].class` as the melee/handling bucket (sim data, untouched); the table is render-only.
tasks.risks: Pure additive draw code, no new cache dimensions, no frame-loop cost — the main risk is stylistic drift: 17 hand-tuned shapes can end up inconsistent in weight. Fix the barrel width and stock tone once as module constants and derive from them. Verify each key renders by staging a row of one soldier per weapon at scale 48 (`sim.addSquadFromDef` variants or direct `soldiers[i].weapon` assignment render-side is not possible — stage via a squad mix and shoot the units crop).

tasks.title: Soldier kit detail tiers: webbing, pack, helmet cover/netting, role and veterancy marks
tasks.detail:
Turns the torso from a flat ellipse with two strap strokes into a kitted man. All inside `torso()`/`helmet()`/new helpers; all tier-gated; the only new cache dimension is a small `variant` byte gated to tier ≥ 2.

**Torso volume (tier ≥ 2).** `torso()` currently fills one flat `k.uniform` ellipse with a 0.035 dark stroke. Add, in order: (a) an edge-darkening radial gradient — `createRadialGradient(0,0,0, 0,0,rx*1.05)` from `k.uniform` at stop 0.55 to `mix(k.uniform,'#000',0.28)` at stop 1, which reads as a rounded back from any facing and is rotation-invariant by construction (the directional signal lives in U2's glint/shadow, never in a baked highlight); (b) a shoulder-seam arc across the upper third at `rgba(0,0,0,0.18)`; (c) a collar tick `0.06` wide at the front edge in `mix(k.uniform,'#000',0.35)`.

**Webbing, per side (tier ≥ 2, replacing `torsoStraps`/`torsoGear`).** US: M1923 cartridge belt as a 0.055-wide band across the waist at `rgba(52,45,30,0.55)` with 5 pouch ticks (0.03 dark separators, clamped to `hair`); haversack 0.13×0.22 rounded rect on the back edge with a horseshoe bedroll arc over its top (tier 3: 3 lashing ticks); canteen ellipse 0.06×0.05 on the right hip; entrenching-tool handle 0.14 line on the pack's left. German: Y-straps as two 0.035 lines converging from the shoulders to a central 0.05 belt buckle dot; two ammo pouches flanking the buckle (0.07×0.05 each); breadbag ellipse 0.07×0.05 at the left rear (already there — keep, add a flap tick); gas-mask canister as a 0.06×0.11 *ribbed* cylinder (3 ticks at tier 3) on the right rear; mess tin square on the pack. MG crews of either side keep the belt fleck across the chest, but at tier ≥ 2 make it a real belt: 6 short perpendicular ticks along the diagonal.

**Helmet (tier ≥ 2/3).** Keep the faction silhouettes exactly as they are (US dome + brim ring, GE ellipse + flared rear skirt — that read works). Add at tier 2: a chinstrap arc `rgba(0,0,0,0.3)` across the lower quarter, and a 0.02 rim of `mix(k.helmet,'#000',0.4)` inside the existing outline for thickness. At tier 3: netting as 3 arcs × 3 chords in `rgba(0,0,0,0.16)` clipped to the dome (US), or a cover-band + two splinter dabs of `rgba(70,74,52,0.5)` (GE). Netting on a 23 px helmet at band 48 is exactly the kind of texture the bake budget exists for; the `hair()` clamp from U1 keeps it from disappearing at band 24, where it should instead be *skipped* (tier 2 draws no netting).

**Role + veterancy marks.** `Soldier.role` (`'leader'|'gunner'|'assistant'|'rifleman'|'bearer'|'driver'|'sniper'|'scout'|'aidman'`) and `Soldier.xp` are both already on the entity and already read render-side. Add `export function kitVariant(role: Role, xp: number, band: number): number` → `tier(band) < 2 ? 0 : (roleBits | (tier(band) >= 3 && xp >= 3 ? 4 : 0))` with roleBits: 0 default, 1 aidman, 2 leader, 3 gunner/assistant. Thread it through `getSprite(side, weapon, pose, frame, band, variant)` and the key string. Marks: **aidman** — white disc r 0.09 on the helmet crown with a red `#8c2018` cross (top-down we see the helmet top, so the crown is the right place, not the side) plus a white brassard tick 0.05 on the left upper arm; **leader** — no netting, a map-case flap 0.09×0.13 on the left hip, binocular case 0.06×0.05 centred on the chest, and one 0.055 pale tick across the rear helmet edge; **gunner/assistant** — a second bandolier diagonal and an ammo-can silhouette 0.1×0.07 riding the pack; **veteran bit** — 3 dark-green foliage dabs (`rgba(58,70,44,0.6)`, r 0.02-0.03) tucked under the helmet net. Apply variants only in the poses where a torso and helmet are actually visible (idle/aim/walk/kneel/prone/melee); pass 0 for dead/dragged/surrendered so those don't multiply.

**Leg/boot read (tier ≥ 3).** The `dot(g, lx, side*0.13, 0.07, '#3a3128')` boots become boot + legging: the dot stays, plus a 0.05-wide `mix(k.trousers,'#000',0.2)` band 0.06 above it, and a 0.03 heel tick behind. Cheap, and it stops the legs reading as pipes.

Renderer hook: `const variant = kitVariant(s.role, s.xp, band)` next to the existing `const band = bandFor(cam.scale)` at renderer.ts:562, passed into `getSprite`. Nothing else in the frame loop changes.
tasks.risks: Cache growth is the real hazard: the variant dimension can multiply the band-48 working set (already ~34 MB) by up to 4. Mitigations are all in the spec — tier gating, pose whitelist for variants, U1's LRU + `spriteCacheStats()`. Check the stats at the units/enemy crops after landing and confirm eviction is not thrashing. Second risk: over-decoration muddying the silhouette pillar (rule 5) — every mark above is inside the torso/helmet outline except the brassard, so the outline is preserved; verify at 24 that the figure still reads as a clean shape and not as noise.

tasks.title: Vehicle surface fidelity: weld/panel bevels, hatches and vents, casemate-turret depth, stowage, mud skirts, weathered markings
tasks.detail:
Vehicles are five flat-rect drawings with one grille and one marking. There are only a handful on a map, so the bake budget per kind is effectively unlimited and the frame cost is zero — this is the cheapest large win after U2.

**Shared helpers (new, all `hair()`-clamped):**
- `weld(g, pts, band)` — the single most important addition: stroke the seam `rgba(0,0,0,0.30)` at `hair`, then re-stroke offset by `+hair` on the sun-perpendicular... no: offset along **+X of bake space** (rotation-invariant fake bevel) in `rgba(255,255,255,0.07)`. Flat plates become plates.
- `bolts(g, x0,y0,x1,y1,n)` — dot row, r = `max(hair, 0.035)`, `rgba(0,0,0,0.28)` with a `rgba(255,255,255,0.06)` 1-px cap at tier 3.
- `hatch(g, cx, cy, r)` — `deck`-toned disc, `rgba(0,0,0,0.3)` rim ring, inner 0.6r arc highlight, hinge tab 0.12×0.06 on the -X side, handle tick.
- `louvre(g, x, y, w, h, n)` — inset dark border + the existing `grilleLines` inside + a bevel on the top edge.
- `plate(g, path, tone)` — fill + weld the outline in one call, so every armour facet is one line of code.
- Stowage kit: `bedroll(x,y,len)` capsule in canvas `#6a6450` with 3 lashing ticks; `jerrycan(x,y)` 0.4×0.28 rounded rect, 3 vertical ribs + an X-brace + dark cap; `crate(x,y)` 0.5×0.4 with 3 plank lines; `tarp(x,y)` 4-point irregular polygon in `#5c5847`; `spareTrack(x,y,n)` n link ticks on the glacis; `towCable(x,y,r)` a 0.04 arc loop. Placement is fixed per kind (deterministic, shared across instances — do NOT add a per-instance weathering dimension; at band 48 a vehicle canvas is 384²×4 ≈ 590 KB and per-instance variants would blow the 24 MB budget for zero legibility gain).

**Per kind:**
- *sherman* — keep the rounded hull; add the three transmission-cover arcs at the front, a cast-texture pair of concentric arcs on the turret, commander's split hatch (two half-discs) + loader's hatch, engine-deck louvre pair replacing the bare `grilleLines`, a .50 cal on the turret roof (0.35 line + 0.12 ammo box), bolt rows along the sponson edges, spare track links on the glacis, bedroll + two jerrycans + a crate on the rear deck, tow cable loop at the rear.
