- *panzer4* — replace the `Schürzen` seam ticks with real skirt plates: a 0.14-thick strip standing outboard of each track, 5 segments with 0.08 gaps, **one segment missing and one bent** (fixed, per-kind — battle-worn is the whole point). Add the turret Schürzen ring as a hexagonal outline around the turret at 1.35r, cupola hatch, rear-deck engine louvres, exhaust muffler cylinder across the rear (0.5×0.18 with two pipe ticks), stowage bin on the turret rear, spare road wheel on the hull side.
- *stug3* — the casemate needs depth, not just an outline: add a Saukopf mantlet blob (0.34×0.28 ellipse over the gun root), the driver's periscope box, two roof hatches, the raised superstructure edge as a `weld` polyline with the lit/shaded pair, side-hull spare track rack (6 links), and a `rgba(0,0,0,0.15)` inset shadow along the -X edge of the casemate where it meets the deck (the one place a rotation-invariant inset AO genuinely reads as height).
- *m3_halftrack* / *sdkfz251* — windscreen visor plates (two 0.5×0.22 rects with 0.03 vision slots), pintle M2 with its shield at the front-right of the bed, bench seat ticks (4 per side), stowed rifles along the bed wall (3 diagonal 0.5 lines), unditching roller at the nose (halftrack only), jerrycans on the rear step. The `sdkfz251` currently falls through to `drawHalftrack` with no faceting — give it the characteristic angled side plates via two `plate()` calls so it is not a US halftrack in feldgrau.

**Mud skirts (tier ≥ 2).** Along both track edges, a `rgba(74,62,44,0.35)` band 0.16 thick whose inner edge is jittered by `hash(kindIndex, i, 31)` (render-side hash per noise.ts, never the sim RNG), heavier over the rear third, plus 6-8 speckle dabs climbing the hull side. This is what stops vehicles looking factory-fresh in a Normandy field.

**Weathered markings (tier ≥ 2).** Keep `star()`/`balkenkreuz()` geometry, then over the top: 4 small `hullTop`-toned ellipses at 0.35 alpha (paint chipping), a `rgba(0,0,0,0.12)` dust wash covering the marking's bounding box, and — at tier ≥ 2 — a turret number via `fillText` (canvas text works fine inside the scaled bake): `g.font = '0.62px ui-sans-serif'`, fixed per kind (`'212'` sherman, `'431'` panzer4, `'S31'` stug3), stroked `rgba(0,0,0,0.5)` then filled `rgba(232,228,216,0.75)`, placed on the turret side / casemate rear. A hand-painted tactical number is a huge authenticity cue for two lines of code.

**Wreck state** — `ashPatches` stays; add at tier ≥ 2: a blown hatch (draw the hatch disc offset 0.4 off its ring), one torn skirt plate, a soot gradient radiating from the turret ring, and the barrel drooping 0.12 off-axis.
tasks.risks: Zero frame-loop cost and few instances, so the only real risks are (a) bake time on the first frame a kind appears at band 48 — measure; if a single bake exceeds ~4 ms, U1's idle prewarm covers the hitch; (b) 590 KB per band-48 canvas × kinds × sides × states against the 24 MB vehicle budget — with no per-instance dimension this lands around 12-24 canvases live, which fits, but re-check after U7 adds the track-phase dimension (×3 on the 'ok' state).

tasks.title: Pose enrichment: live prone crawl, reload read, shouldered aim/kneel, three death sprawls, surrender polish
tasks.detail:
The pose set is broad but each pose is a single frozen picture; the frame budget (6-frame gait) is only spent on walking. All triggers below are render-side reads of existing sim fields — `src/sim/` is untouched.

**1) `crawl` pose, `CRAWL_FRAMES = 4` (the requested prone-crawl frames).** Trigger matters more than the art: `mental === 'pinned'` men provably never move (`sim.ts:2198` — `if (s.path && s.mental !== 'pinned') this.advance(...)`), so a pinned-and-moving trigger would be dead code. The live condition is `shaken`: `s.suppression > 0.35` up to `pinThreshold = 0.7 - (0.5 - courage)*0.2` (sim.ts:2115-2120) still advances. So in `drawSoldier`, insert **before** the `moved > 1e-4` walk branch and after the pinned/prone branch:
```
else if (s.suppression > 0.5 && moved > 1e-4) { pose = 'crawl'; st.phase += moved * 0.9; frame = Math.floor((st.phase % 1) * CRAWL_FRAMES); }
```
Art: reuse `proneBody` with per-frame leg tuples — frame 0 left knee drawn up (`[-0.45,0.08,-0.7,0.28]`) + right leg trailing, frame 1 both mid, frame 2 mirrored, frame 3 mid; the forward arm alternates reach (0.62 → 0.5) with the opposite elbow tucked; weapon dragged alongside at `gun(g, w, 0.42, 0.14, 0.12)`; helmet bobs ±0.02. Per the standing memory lesson, **prove liveness under natural dynamics** before calling it done: instrument a live 247-man battle with a per-pose counter for ~60 s and assert `crawl > 0` without forcing suppression by hand.

**2) `reload` pose (tier ≥ 2), free information already in the sim.** `Soldier.reloading > 0` is a real state nobody renders. Trigger: `else if (s.reloading > 0 && s.targetId >= 0) pose = 'reload'`, placed just before the `targetId >= 0` aim/kneel branch. Art: standing body, weapon canted 0.5 rad down and pulled back to `gx = 0.02`, the support hand up at the receiver (`fx = 0.2, fy = -0.14`), head tipped toward the breech (helmet at `0.02`), and at tier 3 a 0.08 clip/mag tick in the working hand. A squad where you can *see* who is out of the fight is a genuine tactical read, not just decoration.

**3) `aim`/`kneel` shoulder the weapon.** Both currently hold the gun out at arm's length with the head centred. Bring the stock to the cheek: `aim` → `gx 0.10, gy 0.06`, head offset `+0.06` toward the gun side, torso rotated `-0.10` rad (right-shoulder bias), rear elbow tucked (`cap` from `0.02,0.20` to `0.06,0.12`). `kneel` → same shoulder treatment plus a raised rear heel tick and the front knee reading as a distinct 0.075 dot forward of the boot. This is the difference between 'holding a stick' and 'firing a rifle'.

**4) Three death sprawls.** Every corpse in `.screenshots/base-units.png` is the same drawing rotated by a per-id jitter (`renderer.ts:564`). Split `dead` into `dead0` (current sprawl), `dead1` (curled: knees drawn up to the chest, both arms in, head turned — the most common real posture), `dead2` (face-down: arms forward past the head, legs straight, helmet still on and no bare-head/hair dots). Select render-side with `hash(s.id, 0, 7)` from noise.ts (never the sim RNG) → `pose = ('dead' + (h < 0.4 ? 0 : h < 0.75 ? 1 : 2))`. Keep the facing jitter. +2 sprites per (side, weapon); acceptable, and it kills the single most obvious 'procedural' tell on a battlefield full of casualties.

**5) `surrendered` polish.** Two hash-selected variants: hands high (current, but raise the arms further, `0.36,±0.42`, and bow the head — helmet drawn 0.015 smaller with the U2 glint suppressed), and helmet-doffed (bare head `dot(0.04, 0, 0.14, k.skin)` + hair dab, helmet held low in one hand at `0.26,0.2`) plus, at tier 3, a white cloth tick in the raised hand. Also stop baking one surrendered sprite per weapon (U1's key normalisation covers this).

**6) `downed`/`dragged` limp asymmetry (tier ≥ 2).** `Soldier.wounds[]` carries body-part indices. Bucket `wounds[0]` to upper/lower and pick the clutching-hand position accordingly (hand at the chest vs at the thigh) — 2 variants folded into the existing `variant` byte from U4, not a new dimension. Optional; drop it if the cache stats are tight.
tasks.risks: Two traps. First, dead triggers: the crawl condition must be validated on live dynamics (the pinned-never-moves finding above is exactly the failure mode this repo has already been bitten by) — if `suppression > 0.5 && moving` proves rare, lower to 0.4 rather than forcing sim state in a test. Second, keyspace: crawl×4 + dead×3 adds 6 pose-frames per (side, weapon, band) on top of U4's variants; land U1's LRU first and re-read `spriteCacheStats()` at the units crop afterwards.

tasks.title: Vehicle motion: baked track-phase churn, travel-driven dust and track marks, crew and passengers in open tops
tasks.detail:
Vehicles are currently identical whether parked or doing 7 m/s, and an open-topped halftrack shows three anonymous dots regardless of who is aboard. Everything here stays a sprite swap or a decal stamp — no new frame-loop drawing beyond a couple of puffs.

**1) Track shimmer via baked phase variants.** `getVehicleSprite(kind, side, state, band, tphase)` with `tphase ∈ {0,1,2}` and **only** for `state === 'ok'` and `tier(band) >= 2` (pass 0 otherwise so far bands mint nothing). `trackStrip`'s link loop uses `step = 0.32`; offset the loop start by `tphase * step / 3` (0.107). Renderer side, add `private vrs = new Map<number, {px: number, py: number, dist: number}>()` mirroring the soldier `rs` map: per frame `const d = Math.hypot(v.x-px, v.y-py); if (d < 2) st.dist += d;` (the same >2 m teleport guard `drawSoldier` uses), then `const tphase = Math.floor(st.dist / 0.16) % 3`. Critically this is derived from **position, not `now`**, so it freezes correctly under pause like every other sim-derived animation in this renderer. At 4.5 m/s / 60 fps the phase steps roughly every other frame — churn, not strobe.

**2) Travel-driven dust (tier ≥ 2, `cam.scale >= 8`).** Keep a 6-entry ring buffer per vehicle of `{x, y, at}` where `at` is the vehicle's odometer value, pushing one entry every 0.5 m travelled at the two rear track corners (`±(wide/2 - trackH/2)` rotated by facing). Age each puff by `(st.dist - at) / 2.5` in metres, not seconds — pause-safe by construction. Draw as a radial `rgba(150,140,118, 0.14*(1-age))` circle growing 0.6 → 2.0 m. Reuse the smoke gradient idiom already in `drawSmoke`.

**3) Track marks in the decal layer.** Add `DecalLayer.trackMark(x, y, facing)`: two parallel 0.35 m dashes at `±(wide/2 - trackH/2)` in `rgba(58,48,34,0.22)`, `lineWidth 0.42`, with a `Math.random()`-jittered end (decals.ts already documents Math.random as fine there). Stamp from the renderer every 0.7 m of odometer for tracked kinds. At PPM 8 on a 320×240 map this is cheap and gives armour a visible history — the same payoff the crater/blood decals already deliver.

**4) Crew and passengers in open tops.** Soldiers with `inVehicle >= 0` are deliberately not drawn (`renderer.ts:164/172-179` all filter `s.inVehicle < 0`), so the bake is the only place they can appear. Add an `occ` bucket to the cache key for `VEHICLES[kind].openTop` kinds only: count aboard as `crewIds.length + sum(sim.teams[t].memberIds.length for t of v.passengerTeamIds)`, bucket `occ = Math.min(3, Math.floor(n / 3))`. Variants: 0 = empty bed (bench ticks visible), 1 = 2 helmets + shoulders, 2 = 5, 3 = 9 packed. Draw each occupant as a real mini figure, not a dot: helmet using the faction `helmet()` silhouette at 0.62 scale, a shoulder capsule in `hullTop`-contrasting uniform tone, and alternating facing (outboard left/right) so the bed reads as men rather than a grid. Always draw the driver behind the windscreen and, when `crewIds.length > 0`, a gunner standing at the pintle with the MG42/M1919 silhouette from U3's table — the gunner is the silhouette that makes a halftrack read as crewed at 24 px/m. Wrecks draw no occupants (already `if (!wreck)`).

Hook points: `drawVehicle` at renderer.ts:346-359 gains the `vrs` update, the `tphase`/`occ` arguments, the dust ring and the decal stamp; the sprite draw itself stays one `drawImage`.
tasks.risks: The track-phase dimension multiplies live 'ok' vehicle canvases by 3 (590 KB each at band 48) and `occ` multiplies open tops by up to 4 — together that can approach U1's 24 MB vehicle budget if a map fields all five kinds on both sides. Gate both to tier ≥ 2 as specced, bake phases lazily (only when something actually moves), and check `spriteCacheStats()` on the new vehicles crop. Second risk: dust and track marks accumulating into visual noise on a long battle — cap the dust ring at 6 and pick the decal alpha low (0.22) so overlapping passes darken gracefully rather than smearing to mud.

tasks.title: Emplacement bakes: MG on tripod/Lafette, mortars, AT guns — replace the 3-primitive placeholder glyph
tasks.detail:
`drawEmplacement` (renderer.ts:388-418) is a per-frame vector glyph: one filled circle, one line, a dashed team stroke, and a footprint radius computed as `Math.max(2.5, cam.scale * 0.34 * 0.4 * 10)` — an unexplained constant that reduces to `cam.scale * 1.36`. Six emplacement kinds (`m1919_tripod`, `mg42_lafette`, `mortar60`, `mortar81`, `at57`, `pak40`) all render as the same dot-with-a-stick, which is indefensible given a dug-in MG42 or a PaK 40 is the most consequential thing on the map. This is the last unbaked unit class.

**New module** `src/render/emplacements.ts`, mirroring vehicles.ts exactly: `EMPLACEMENT_SPAN = 4` metres, `BANDS = [6,12,24,48]`, `emplacementBandFor(scale)`, `getEmplacementSprite(kind: EmplacementKey, side: Side, state: 'packed'|'deployed', band: number)`, LRU cache from U1, team rim via the same `teamRim` treatment (extract it from vehicles.ts into a shared helper rather than duplicating), and the U2 shadow-silhouette companion (`off` 0.35 m, `stretch` 1.1).

**Critical scoping constraint:** emplacement crews have `inEmplacement >= 0` but `inVehicle < 0`, so they **are** already drawn as individual soldier sprites by the main soldier passes. Do NOT bake crew figures into these sprites (unlike U7's open-top vehicles, where crew are hidden and the bake is their only representation). Bake the weapon and its mount only.

**Per kind, deployed:**
- `m1919_tripod` — tripod as 3 legs 0.9 m from a central pintle dot (two legs forward at ±40°, one trailing), gun body 0.9 m with a 5-tick perforated jacket, pintle traverse ring, belt curving from the feed tray to a 0.4×0.25 ammo can set 0.35 m to the loader's side, a spare-barrel tube alongside.
- `mg42_lafette` — heavier sled mount: a T-frame with two 0.55 m outriggers, a recoil-slide rail under the receiver, the MG42 silhouette from U3 (7-tick fat jacket, muzzle booster), a 0.14×0.1 optic block on the left, drum + belt to two ammo cans.
- `mortar60` / `mortar81` — 0.5 m disc / 0.6 m square baseplate with a socket dot, bipod as a V opening 0.55 m toward the front, tube drawn foreshortened for a high angle (0.55 m / 0.7 m of visible length — a near-vertical tube is *short* from above; that foreshortening is the whole read) with a muzzle-ring bulb, elevation screw tick, plus a 3-shell rack (0.09 dots with 0.05 fin ticks) beside the pit and a `rgba(0,0,0,0.18)` pit ring under the baseplate.
- `at57` / `pak40` — split trail as two 1.6 m legs at ±25° with 0.12 spade ends, two wheels r 0.42 (6 spokes at tier 3, solid disc below), gun shield as a 1.6×0.15 plate angled across the front with a `weld` bevel and a gunner's sight notch, barrel 2.6 m / 3.1 m (PaK 40 gets a 2-baffle muzzle brake, the 57 mm a plain bore), recuperator cylinder riding above the barrel, breech block at the trail junction, and 2 ammo crates + 3 loose shell casings beside the left trail.
- **`state === 'packed'`:** AT guns limber up — trails folded together, barrel at 0.7× visible length, wheels forward; MGs and mortars become a load pile of 2-3 bundles matching `def.loads` (`tripod_m1919`/`lafette` bundle, `mg_gun` tube, `ammo_cans` box; `mortar_tube`/`mortar_baseplate`/`shell_load`). Keep the existing dashed-outline convention for `state !== 'deployed'` in the frame loop so the setup/teardown state stays legible, but draw it as a dashed rounded-rect around the sprite footprint rather than around the old glyph circle.

**Renderer hook:** replace the body of `drawEmplacement` with the vehicle pattern — `pad = EMPLACEMENT_SPAN * cam.scale`, cull, `save/translate/rotate(e.facing)/drawImage/restore`, then the existing selection ring (keep the `sim.teams[e.crewTeamId].squadId` selection test verbatim) and the dashed non-deployed outline. Add the emplacement pass to U2's `drawUnitShadows`. Add a `guns` crop to `scripts/lib/stage.mjs` staging one of each kind on two headings via `sim.addEmplacement(side, kind, x, y, facing, 'deployed')` plus one `'packed'`, and register it in sweep.mjs.
tasks.risks: Low: few instances, no frame-loop cost beyond the one drawImage that replaces several vector calls (likely a small net win). Watch two things — the mortar tube's foreshortened length is easy to get wrong and read as a broken barrel (compare against the AT barrel at the same scale on the new crop), and `EMPLACEMENT_SPAN = 4` must actually contain a PaK 40's 3.1 m barrel plus trails plus the shadow offset; if it clips, raise the span rather than shortening the gun.

effects.summary: Coverage is broad but construction is thin: every transient is a live `createRadialGradient` + `arc` + `fill` per particle, drawn source-over in one flat pass, so nothing has value separation, glow falloff, or mass. The staged capture `.screenshots/design-boom.png` (peak frame, 49 ms) proves the worst of it — inside one boom iteration renderer.ts draws the hot fireball (age<150 ms), then paints the 1.5 s tan ground-dust disc (alpha 0.28) and the smoke column's first puff (whose `start = i*200` makes i=0 begin at age 0) directly over it, so the peak of an explosion reads as a flat pale-tan pancake with an orange fringe and a 2 px geometric ring. The tracer capture shows the muzzle flash as three equal-length straight spikes — a UI arrowhead glyph, not a flash — and renderer.ts:718-720 asserts "ShotEvent carries no weapon field... a per-shot hash stands in", but sim.ts:248 has carried `weapon?: WeaponKey` since the audio pass and audio.ts:176 already consumes it, so per-weapon-class flash variety is available today at zero sim cost. Genuinely absent: debris with mass, shockwave volume, ricochet/masonry, casings, recoil, fires beyond three hand-rolled vehicle puffs, and any ambient layer at all. Only three things need sim work, all one-field additions with no reads and no behavior change: blast radius on `pendingBooms` (`p.fragRadius` is already in scope at sim.ts:1754), `shooterId` on `ShotEvent`, and `deathCause`/`deathDir` on `Soldier` — the determinism hash is an explicit field allow-list (sim.ts:3350-3430), so render-only fields cannot perturb it.

tasks.title: fx.ts foundation: baked particle atlas, additive hot pass, wind, ballistic helper, zoom tiers
tasks.detail:
New `src/render/fx.ts`. This is the enabler for FX2-FX7 and it is also the perf budget that pays for them: today every smoke puff calls `createRadialGradient` + `arc` + `fill` per particle per frame (drawSmoke: 3-5 per sim.smoke entry; each boom: 3 more), and gradient objects are not cached by any browser. Replace all of it with bake-once/drawImage-per-particle, exactly the pattern dudes.ts already uses.

(1) BAKED ATLAS. `getFx(kind, px)` with a `Map<string, HTMLCanvasElement>` keyed `kind|px`, mirroring `getSprite` in dudes.ts. Bake at two fixed pixel sizes (32, 96) and let drawImage scale — a scaled radial-gradient bake is visually indistinguishable from a live gradient. Kinds and stops: `smoke` rgba(152,154,152) a=1→0.55@0.6→0; `dustTan` rgba(150,130,100); `masonry` rgba(196,190,176); `soot` rgba(34,31,27) (near-black, for brew-ups); `flash` rgba(255,252,238)→rgba(255,196,96,0.5)@0.45→0; `fire` rgba(255,186,84)→rgba(214,96,32,0.6)@0.5→0; `ring` annulus (stops 0:transparent, 0.62:transparent, 0.80:opaque, 1:transparent); `spark` 8 px hot dot; `leaf` 8 px green fleck; `chunk0..3` 12 px irregular 5-7-vertex polygons fill `#3b3226` + 1 px darker rim; `casing` 8 px brass sliver (2x5 rounded rect `#8e7434` body, `#c9ab5e` NW highlight); `pock0..3` 16 px — irregular dark core rgba(28,22,16,0.72) r≈5 px, pale spall crescent rgba(210,204,188,0.5) offset OPPOSITE `SUN` from light.ts so chips catch the one sun, plus 2 chips; `hazeBand` 256x64 soft strip. Use `Math.random` inside bakes (bake-time, per the invariant) but seed variant selection at call sites from `hash()`.

(2) `blit(ctx, kind, sx, sy, rPx, alpha, rot = 0)` — sets `globalAlpha`, one centered `drawImage` at `2*rPx` square, `save/rotate/restore` ONLY when `rot !== 0` (chunks, casings, pocks). Restore alpha to 1 on exit.

(3) `export const WIND = { dx: 0.93, dy: -0.37, speed: 1.6 }` — one unit vector + m/s, shared by smoke drift, ember rise, haze scroll, plume lean, leaf fall. Comment cross-referencing light.ts: the sun model owns direction of light, this owns direction of air; keeping them separate axes (SUN is SE, WIND is ENE) stops the scene reading as one big diagonal.

(4) `hotPass(ctx, f)` = `save(); globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter'; f(); restore()`. Every additive draw in the codebase batches into ONE call per frame so the GCO flips twice, never per particle.

(5) `ballistic(t, v, vz)` → `[dist, z]` with `dist = v*t`, `z = Math.max(0, vz*t - 4.9*t*t)`. Standard top-down 3D cheat: ground position = origin + dir*dist, sprite drawn at `(sx, sy - z*cam.scale*0.9)`, shadow ellipse at `(sx, sy)` alpha `0.18*(1 - Math.min(1, z/2))`. Serves debris chunks and shell casings.

(6) `export function fxDetail(scale: number): 0 | 1 | 2 { return scale >= 24 ? 2 : scale >= 10 ? 1 : 0; }` — tier 2 = full (casings, pockmarks, per-lick flame), tier 1 = mid (chunks, sparks, plumes, birds), tier 0 = silhouette only (fireball + smoke mass, zero sub-particles). Every effect below multiplies its particle count by the tier so a zoomed-out battle never pays for invisible detail. This is how detail scales WITH the existing zoom-band system rather than fighting it.

(7) Migrate the two existing gradient hot spots to `blit` with zero visual intent change: `drawSmoke` (renderer.ts:264-271) and the boom ground dust (renderer.ts:891-897). Land this as its own commit — it shifts every pixel in the vfx contact sheet, and the diff must be attributable before FX2 changes intent on top of it.
tasks.risks: Swapping live gradients for baked blits moves every existing effect's pixels, so the vfx.mjs and sweep.mjs baselines all shift at once — commit alone, re-shoot both contact sheets, eyeball before proceeding. Bake memory is small (~15 sprites x 2 sizes) but the atlas must be lazily built, never eagerly, or first-frame cost spikes. `globalAlpha` leakage is the classic bug: assert it is 1 at the end of Renderer.draw during development.

tasks.title: Explosion rebuild: layered flash/fireball/soot shell/debris/shockwave, correct compositing order, scaled by blast radius
tasks.detail:
SIM-EVENT: `pendingBooms` gains a blast-radius field. At sim.ts:1754 inside `explode`, `p.fragRadius` is already in scope — change to `this.pendingBooms.push({ x, y, r: p.fragRadius })` (3 for GRENADE_BLAST, 9 for the mortar/barrage default). At sim.ts:1972 (vehicle brew-up, which does not route through `explode`) push `{ x: v.x, y: v.y, r: 6 }`. Widen the field type to `{ x: number; y: number; r?: number }[]` and the `takeBooms()` return type (sim.ts:1550). Nothing in sim reads `r`; no tick work; zero behavior change.

Renderer: `Boom` gains `r`, `const rs = Math.min(1.2, Math.max(0.33, (b.r ?? 9) / 9))`. Every radius and count below scales by `rs`.

ROOT FIX FIRST — the compositing order. Today, per boom per frame, the order is ring → fireball(150 ms) → ejecta → **ground-dust disc (1.5 s, alpha 0.28 tan)** → **smoke column (first puff starts at age 0)**. The last two paint over the hot core, which is exactly why design-boom.png at 49 ms is a flat pale-tan pancake. New per-frame order inside each boom: compression ring → ground dust RING → soot shell → fireball lobes → ejecta → debris (+shadows) → smoke column; then all additive elements (flash, fireball core, sparks) drawn last inside a single `hotPass`.

TIMELINE (all wall-clock, BOOM_MS → 2600):
- 0-45 ms `flash`: additive, r `(0.5 + 3.2*t)*rs*scale`, alpha `1-t`. The white-hot instant the current code has no equivalent of.
- 30-90 ms compression: `ring` blit at rgba(30,24,16), r `0.7→2.9*rs*scale`, alpha `0.25→0`, drawn UNDER everything — a beat of darkening before the dust ring, which is what makes a blast feel like it displaces air.
- 40-380 ms shockwave: `ring` blit tan, r `0.8→4.6*rs*scale`, alpha `0.55→0`, edge softening by scaling the ring sprite (never a 2 px `stroke()` circle — that is the arcade read to kill).
- 60-900 ms soot shell (NEW, drawn BEFORE the fireball every frame): 4 `soot` blits at `hash(sx,sy,110+i)*2π`, dist `(0.3+0.6*hash)*rs*scale`, r `(1.0+t*2.2)*rs*scale`, alpha `0.5*(1-t)`. The fireball then punches through it — dark-around-bright is the entire reason a real explosion reads at a glance.
- 30-260 ms fireball: 3 asymmetric lobes, lobe i delayed `i*22 ms`, offset at `hash(sx,sy,100+i)*2π` by `(0.15+0.35*hash)*rs*scale`, r `(0.7+t*2.4)*rs*scale`, alpha `(1-t)^0.7`, source-over `fire` sprite; plus ONE additive `fire` at the innermost lobe at 0.55 r inside the hot pass. Asymmetry is what stops it reading as a disc.
- 0-420 ms ejecta: keep the existing 8-12 streaks but add gravity droop (`+t*t*0.9*cam.scale` on y at the far end) and taper lineWidth 0.09→0.02.
- 60-1600 ms DEBRIS CHUNKS (tier>=1): `n = Math.round((6 + hash*6) * rs * tier)`; per chunk v `6+hash*10` m/s, vz `3.5+hash*5`, sprite `chunk[hash&3]`, rotation `t*(4+hash*8)` rad, positioned via `ballistic()` with its shadow ellipse. On landing (z reaches 0) call a new `decals.grit(x, y)` — a 0.12-0.3 m dark speck + 2 flecks, `Math.random` fine in decal code. Chunks with real arcs and ground shadows are the single biggest "this has mass" upgrade available.
- 150-1400 ms ground dust: an expanding tan `ring` (r `1.2→4.5*rs*scale`, alpha `0.30→0`), NOT the current filled disc. Keep one small filled `dustTan` at the base but cap it at alpha 0.14 and r `1.6*rs` so it can never wash the fireball again.
- 200-2600 ms smoke column: `n = 4 + Math.round(2*rs)`, puff i starts at `200 + i*180 ms`; climb `pt*4.2*rs*cam.scale` in screen -y; lean `WIND.dx * WIND.speed * ptSec * cam.scale` (replacing the current `Math.sin(sx*0.01 + i)` fudge, which drifts each boom a different arbitrary way); r `(0.9+pt*2.2)*rs`; alpha `(1-pt)*0.42`; tone lerps `soot`→`smoke` over the first 400 ms because fire-smoke starts black and greys as it cools.

SPILLOVER WINS from the same field: (a) `worldShake` (renderer.ts:204-216) scales trauma by `0.45 + 0.55*rs` so a grenade stops jolting the camera like a barrage shell; (b) `decals.scorch(x, y, rs)` gains a radius multiplier so grenade craters stop being the same size as 81 mm craters.
tasks.risks: Additive `lighter` on a deliberately desaturated palette is the one place this pass can break 'Muted Normandy' — keep additive strictly to the sub-260 ms window and to small radii, and screenshot-check the 49 ms and 150 ms buckets against the current sheet before/after. The soot shell can read as a grey blob if its alpha creeps above ~0.55 at the peak. BOOM_MS 2000→2600 means the vfx.mjs static captures' 2200 ms settle wait (scripts/vfx.mjs:58) is now too short and will photobomb the death-pose shot — bump it to 2800 in the same commit.

tasks.title: Tracers + muzzle flash driven by the real weapon field: per-class geometry, glow falloff, back-blast, tracer-round ratio, ricochet sparks
tasks.detail:
NO sim change. Delete the stale comment at renderer.ts:718-720 and the `shotHash`-as-size-classifier: `ShotEvent.weapon` exists (sim.ts:248), is populated at every small-arms/emplacement/grenade emit site (sim.ts:1219, 2037, 2372, 3240), and audio.ts:176 already consumes it. Keep `hash()` only for jitter.

CLASSIFY IN fx.ts, not from `WEAPONS[w].class` — data.ts buckets bazooka, panzerfaust, mortar60 and pak40_gun all as `class:'rifle'`, which would give a Panzerfaust a rifle flash. Explicit table `FLASH: Record<WeaponKey | 'cannon', {r, spikes, len, spread, life, tracerW, tracerCol, extra}>`:
- rifle (garand/carbine/kar98k/springfield/kar98k_scoped/bar): r 0.30 m, 2 spikes, len 1.35xr, spread 0.42, life 50 ms, 1 px pale-straw thread.
- smg (thompson/mp40): r 0.22 m, 3 short spikes, len 1.0xr, spread 0.80, life 38 ms.
- mg (m1919/mg42): r 0.42 m, 3 spikes, len 1.8xr, spread 0.30, life 70 ms, 2 px warmer thread, PLUS a second flash at 40% alpha 25 ms later — the belt-rhythm double-beat that makes an MG read as an MG at a glance.
- rocket (bazooka/schreck/panzerfaust): r 0.70 m, no spikes, big additive bloom, PLUS a 400 ms back-blast cone opposite the bearing (5 `smoke` blits along -u, r 0.6→1.8 m, dist 0.4→2.2 m, alpha 0.45→0, ±0.4 rad fan). The most characteristic WW2 silhouette the game currently doesn't have.
- cannon (mortar60/mortar81/at57_gun/pak40_gun AND `weapon === undefined`): r 0.85 m, 2 spikes, life 110 ms, additive bloom, PLUS a 700 ms muzzle-blast ground wash ahead (3 `dustTan` blits in a ±0.35 rad cone, 1.5-4 m out, alpha 0.35→0) — the dust signature that gives away a gun position.

KILL THE ARROWHEAD. renderer.ts:740-746 draws three equal-length straight spikes at exactly ±0.55 rad, which reads as a UI arrow glyph (visible in .screenshots/design-tracer.png). Replace with: (a) an ORIENTED TEARDROP core — `save(); translate(mx,my); rotate(atan2(uy,ux)); scale(1.15, 0.62); blit('flash', 0.45*fr, 0, fr, fa); restore()` — the flash must be longer along the barrel than across it; (b) spikes at UNEQUAL hash-jittered lengths `(0.55 + hash*0.45) * spikeLen` and angles `spread * (0.7 + hash*0.6)` with lineWidth tapering to 0 at the tip. Asymmetry is the whole fix.

GLOW FALLOFF: add a wide low-alpha `flash` blit at 2.4x fr, alpha 0.22, additive — the soft outer falloff the current hard-stop gradient (`rgba(255,150,40,0)` at 1.0) has none of.

TRACER ROUNDS: only ~1-in-5 shots (`hash(...) < 0.2`, or 1-in-3 for mg class) get a visible tracer; the rest get only the faint thread. Real belts were 1-in-5 and the resulting irregular rhythm is what makes sustained fire read right — uniform tracers on every round is the arcade tell. For a tracer round: keep the 90 ms travel but give it a head (`spark` blit at the leading point, additive, min 1 px) and a tail (3-stop linear gradient stroke, transparent at segStart to full at travelT), and shorten the trailing window from 0.18 to 0.11 of the path so it reads as a round in flight, not a dash.

RICOCHET SPARKS (tier>=1): on a hit against a target in cover, and on every hard-surface strike from FX4, spawn 2-4 `spark` particles on `ballistic()` arcs (v 4-9 m/s, vz 2-5, life 260 ms) fanned ±1.1 rad around the reflected bearing (i.e. back toward the shooter), additive, fading warm→dark.

RESTRUCTURE: split the `this.tracers` loop in `drawFire` into a cool pass (threads, impact dust, blood) and one `hotPass` (all flashes, glow halos, tracer heads, sparks, kill flash) so GCO flips twice per frame rather than once per particle.
tasks.risks: The 1-in-5 tracer ratio makes the vfx.mjs shot triggers non-deterministic in appearance unless the harness pins the hash inputs — stage the gate rows at fixed fx/fy/tx/ty so the hash lands the same every run, and add one explicit tracer-round row and one thread-only row. Additive flashes at 247 soldiers means potentially hundreds of `lighter` draws per frame: the single batched hotPass is load-bearing for the >=100 fps floor, and the count must still be capped (skip flashes for off-screen shooters before the pass, which the existing `place`-style cull does not currently do for tracers).

tasks.title: Wall/masonry strikes with overshoot raycast + persistent pockmark layer (marks.ts)
tasks.detail:
NO sim change. Two parts.

(A) NEW `src/render/marks.ts` — a capped, world-space, viewport-culled fine-detail stamp layer, the crisp complement to DecalLayer (whose PPM=8 makes a 0.1 m pockmark 0.8 px — too coarse; and a higher-PPM canvas for a 320x240 map is 100s of MB, so a canvas is the wrong tool here). `MarkLayer`: fixed-capacity ring buffer `CAP = 640` of `{ x, y, rot, kind }`; `add(kind, x, y, rot)` guarded by a 0.5 m-cell density map (`Map<number, number>` keyed `(cy*1024 + cx)`, max 6 marks per cell, silently dropped past that — clustering, not caking); `draw(ctx, cam, cw, ch)` culls to the viewport +1 m, early-returns when `fxDetail(cam.scale) < 1`, and blits the baked `pock*/casing/grit/spatter` sprites at world scale (one drawImage per mark, ~40-150 visible in a live fight). Call it from `Renderer.draw` immediately after `this.decals.draw(...)` (renderer.ts:135) so marks land over the terrain chunks — including the baked wall strokes from `drawEdge` (terrain.ts:502) — and under soldiers. One layer, one cap, one cull, reused by FX6 casings and FX6 blood spatter.

(B) OVERSHOOT RAYCAST — `traceOvershoot(map, fx, fy, tx, ty, h)` in fx.ts. Rationale, because the obvious design is wrong: the sim already cleared LOS before firing, so there is NEVER a full wall between shooter and target; a missed round must be resolved PAST the target. Today every miss puffs earth-brown dust at the target's feet (renderer.ts:776-793), which reads as the round hitting dirt beneath a man standing in a window. Instead: jitter the bearing by `(h - 0.5) * 0.08` rad, march from (tx,ty) outward in 0.25 m steps up to 12 m (48 iterations max) against `sim.map`; at each tile-boundary crossing test the crossed `hEdge(x,y)` / `vEdge(x,y)`. First `EDGE.WALL` or `EDGE.WINDOW` → `{ kind: 'wall', x, y, nx, ny }` (normal from which axis was crossed). Else first tile whose `terrainKeyAt` is `hedge` or `woods` → `{ kind: 'foliage' }`. Else `{ kind: 'ground' }` at `1.5 + h*2.5` m past. Run only when `!t.hit`, the segment midpoint is on-screen, and `fxDetail >= 1`. Cost at 247 soldiers is ~60 shots/s x <=48 edge tests — negligible.

VISUALS. Wall strike: 3-5 `masonry` blits (pale rgba(196,190,176) — deliberately a different VALUE and hue family from the earth-brown ground dust, so a player can tell masonry from dirt without reading position) in a cone off the wall normal, r 0.10→0.35 m over 260 ms, alpha 0.6→0; 1-2 `chunk` fragments on a short `ballistic()` hop (v 3-6, vz 2-4, 300 ms); 2-3 additive `spark`s per FX3; and hash-gated 1-in-3, `marks.add('pock', x, y, wallAngle)`. Foliage strike: 3-4 `leaf` blits drifting on WIND with a downward bias, 400 ms, 1-in-6 `marks.add('grit')`. Ground strike: the existing 3-particle dust, but relocated to the real overshoot point, upgraded to `dustTan` blits, 1-in-8 `marks.add('grit')`.

POCKMARK ART (baked in FX1): 16 px — irregular 5-vertex dark core rgba(28,22,16,0.72) at r≈5 px, a pale spall crescent rgba(210,204,188,0.5) offset OPPOSITE `SUN` (light.ts) so every chip catches the one sun, plus 2 tiny radial chips. 4 variants selected by hash. Drawn at 0.11 m so a contested wall accumulates a believable spread of small strikes rather than one growing smudge.
tasks.risks: Density guard and CAP are load-bearing: a 10-minute firefight against one farmhouse would otherwise post thousands of marks and either tank the frame or turn the wall black. The raycast must use the same edge-crossing convention as map.ts `canStep` (renderer.ts:118-125 shows the vEdge(x1,y0) / hEdge(x0,y1) asymmetry) or marks will land one tile off — write a unit test that fires a known ray at a known wall edge and asserts the hit coordinate. Marks drawn after decals means they also sit over blood pools; check that a pockmark stamped on open ground (grit) does not read as a floating speck at 48 px/m.

tasks.title: Burning buildings and vehicle brew-ups: flame licks, ember drift, sooty plumes, warm ground pool
tasks.detail:
NO sim change — building fire is render-derived from booms landing on building tiles. `private fires = new Map<number, { x: number; y: number; tick: number; intensity: number }>()`, keyed by `sim.map.buildingIdAt(Math.floor(b.x), Math.floor(b.y))` for buildings and by `-1000 - v.id` for vehicles, so one draw routine serves both.

IGNITION: in `addBooms`, if `bid >= 0`, `fires.set(bid, { x, y, tick: sim.tick, intensity: Math.min(1, (prev?.intensity ?? 0) + 0.45) })`. For vehicles, create/refresh the entry on every frame `v.burning` is true, alongside the existing `deadVehicles` scorch latch (renderer.ts:350-353), so a burning tank never times out while the sim still says it burns.

CLOCKS — state the split deliberately, it is not an oversight. LIFETIME runs on `sim.tick` (the `barrageMarks` precedent at renderer.ts:311): `ageSec = (sim.tick - f.tick) / 30`, alive for 90 s, `intensity` fading over the final 25 s, deleted after. Pausing the game must not burn a house down. FLICKER runs on wall-clock `now`, matching the existing vehicle burning puffs (renderer.ts:371 already animates under pause) — 30 Hz sim sampling would visibly step a flame.

DRAW — new `drawFires(ctx, cam, now, cw, ch)` called AFTER `this.roofs.drawTops(...)` (renderer.ts:187) so flames sit over the roof they are consuming, and before `drawSmoke`.
- Licks: `n = 2 + Math.round(3 * intensity * tier)` at hash-anchored offsets within ±1.4 m, clamped inside the building rect from `sim.buildings` (`{x,y,w,h}`) when the key is a building. Per lick, `flick = 0.5 + 0.5*Math.sin(now*0.0075*(7 + hash*4) + hash*6.28)`; `blit('fire', x, y - (0.35 + 0.5*flick)*scale, (0.30 + 0.22*flick)*intensity*scale)` source-over, plus one additive `flash` at 0.4x r inside the frame's hot pass.
- The value pair that makes fire read top-down: immediately above each lick, a `soot` blit at 1.6x r, alpha 0.30. Bright core with dark smoke directly over it, never bright alone.
- Embers (tier>=1): a pool of <=8 per fire, `t = ((now*0.001 + i*0.37) % life) / life` with `life = 1.6 + hash*1.2`; position = lick base + `WIND * WIND.speed * 1.9 * t`, rise `t*2.6*scale`; additive `spark`, r 0.05→0.02 m, alpha `(1-t)^1.6 * 0.8`.
- Plume: 3 blits rising 5.5 m over a 3.2 s wrapping wall-clock phase, leaning on WIND, r 0.9→3.2 m, alpha 0.34→0. Buildings use grey-brown `smoke`; VEHICLES use `soot` for the first 60% of the plume — a brewed-up tank is the sootiest thing on a WW2 field and that near-black column against pale ground is free readability at any zoom, including below the sprite LOD threshold.
- Warm ground pool: one additive `fire` blit at the fire centre, r `3.2 * intensity` m, alpha 0.09. FLAG FOR ART-DIRECTION SIGN-OFF: this is a second light source. It is a light POOL only — no cast-shadow direction changes anywhere — so it should not violate 'one sun', but if rejected, delete this single blit and the rest of the task stands unchanged.
- Replace the three hand-rolled puffs in `drawVehicle` (renderer.ts:367-382) entirely with the shared routine.
tasks.risks: The warm ground pool is the one element that can break the 'one sun / muted' direction — build it behind a constant that can be zeroed. A village hit by a full barrage could light 6-8 buildings at once; cap concurrent fires at 12 (drop the oldest by tick) and verify frame time with the boom-heavy staging. Fires drawn above roofs means a fire in a building the player has not seen will render through fog of war — gate the whole entry on `sim.sideSeesPoint('blue', f.x, f.y)` the way main.ts:910 gates unit events, or a burning house becomes an intel leak.

tasks.title: SIM-EVENT: recoil kick, shell casings, directional death poses, and tasteful wound feedback
tasks.detail:
This is the feel-ceiling from docs/plans/2026-07-23-feel-events-design.md. Two minimal sim additions, both write-only.

SIM-EVENT (a): `ShotEvent` gains `shooterId: number` (sim.ts:241). Emit sites and their in-scope value: 2037 `resolveSmallArmsShot` — thread an id param from its callers (2048 has `shooter.id`, 2043 vehicle MG passes -1); 1219 emplacement — the firing crewman from `pickFirer`, else -1; 1884/1945 vehicle — -1; 2372 grenade throw — `s.id`; 3240 hip-fire — `s.id`. Nothing in sim reads it. Renderer treats -1/undefined as 'no shooter' and skips recoil.

SIM-EVENT (b): `Soldier` gains `deathCause?: 'shot' | 'boom' | 'melee'` and `deathDirX?: number; deathDirY?: number`, written once at each kill site from data already in scope (shot bearing / soldier-minus-boom delta / attacker-minus-victim delta). Corpses persist and get discovered later through fog, which is exactly why this must live on the record and not in a transient event. The determinism hash is an explicit field allow-list (sim.ts:3350-3391 lists every soldier column by name), so these fields cannot perturb it — but verify that row is still explicit before landing.

RECOIL (renderer): `RState` gains `rkx, rky, rUntil`. On each visible event with `shooterId >= 0`: `rUntil = now + 110`, `rkx = -ux * amp`, `rky = -uy * amp`, with `amp` in metres by FX3's class — mg 0.16, rifle 0.11, smg 0.07, rocket 0.20, cannon 0.24. In `drawSoldier`, `k = st.rUntil > now ? ((st.rUntil - now)/110) ** 2 : 0`; offset the sprite translate by `st.rkx*k*cam.scale, st.rky*k*cam.scale` and add `0.045*k` (hash-signed) to `st.facing` for muzzle rise. Wall-clock, so it decays under pause exactly like tracers.

CASINGS — NO sim change needed: the ejection point is `(fx, fy)` and the bearing is `fx→tx`, both already on the event. `private casings: { x, y, dir, v, vz, at, rot }[]`, cap 140 FIFO, spawned only at `fxDetail >= 2` (>=24 px/m — below that a casing is sub-pixel) and only for visible shooters. Count by class: rifle 1, smg 1, mg 2, rocket/cannon 0. Eject 90 deg right of the bearing ±0.35 rad, v 1.6-3.0 m/s, vz 1.8-2.6, tumble `rot += 14 rad/s`, positioned by `ballistic()` with its shadow ellipse. On landing (~430 ms) hand off to `marks.add('casing', x, y, rot)`. Brass accumulating around a machine-gun nest sells a sustained position better than any amount of flash work.

DEATH POSES (dudes.ts): add `'dead_thrown'` (torso displaced +X, arms and legs trailing -X, helmet flung far, no bayonet) and `'dead_tangled'` (curled, one knee up, weapon under the body) to `Pose`; both reuse `deadKit(k)` and carry no team rim, matching the existing `dead` case. Renderer pose select: `pose = s.deathCause === 'boom' ? 'dead_thrown' : s.deathCause === 'melee' ? 'dead_tangled' : 'dead'`. Facing: replace the current `st.facing + ((s.id*2654435761)%100)/100 - 0.5` jitter (renderer.ts:564) with `Math.atan2(s.deathDirY, s.deathDirX)` plus ±0.25 rad hash jitter WHEN THE FIELDS EXIST, keeping the exact current expression when they do not (old saves, coarse resolver — the renderer must not assume presence). For `'boom'`, additionally displace the drawn position by `dir * (0.4 + hash*0.7)` m: thrown bodies do not lie where they stood. Sprite cache keys already include `pose`, so this is 2 extra bakes per (side, weapon, band).

BLOOD — folded here because it rides the same event. On `hit && !kill`: 4-6 dark-maroon flecks (`rgba(74,13,10,0.5)`) in a 55 deg cone continuing PAST the victim along the bearing, 180 ms; plus hash-gated 1-in-2, 2-3 `marks.add('spatter')` at 0.3-0.9 m downrange. On `kill`: 5-8 flecks, a 4-sliver spatter fan, and the existing `decals.pool`. Hard limits, non-negotiable: nothing brighter in value than #5c0f0c, no chunks, no arterial spurt, no alpha above 0.5, and everything behind the same `soldierVisibleTo` FOW gate the melee path already applies (renderer.ts:84-86) — which the shot path currently does NOT have.
tasks.risks: The only task touching src/sim/ — keep both diffs to field declarations plus write-only assignments at sites that already exist, run `npm test` (198 tests) before and after, and confirm the replay/determinism hash is byte-identical on seed 7. Threading `shooterId` through `resolveSmallArmsShot` touches four callers including the vehicle MG path; get the -1 sentinel right or the renderer will recoil the wrong soldier. Casings at >=24 px/m across a whole MG team can hit the 140 cap fast — verify FIFO eviction does not strobe. Blood is the one place where 'more fidelity' is actively wrong: hold the constants above.

tasks.title: Ambient atmosphere: drifting haze bands, dust motes, wind-leaned smoke, startled birds
tasks.detail:
NO sim change. Four cheap layers that make the field feel occupied rather than staged.

HAZE BANDS: use the baked `hazeBand` sprite (256x64, vertical soft gradient to rgba(201,196,180,0.5) at centre, plus 12 hash-placed soft blobs for lumpiness) rather than full-viewport pattern fills — bands are both cheaper and more painterly than a uniform wash. `private haze` = 5 world-anchored bands `{ y, len, hgt, phase, a }` generated ONCE from `hash(map.w, map.h, i)`: `len` 70-140 m, `hgt` 9-24 m, `a` 0.035-0.075. One `drawImage` per band per frame; x offset `= ((band.phase + WIND.dx*WIND.speed*0.06*now/1000) % (map.w + len)) - len`, y drifts on `WIND.dy`. Draw after decals/marks, BEFORE soldiers (haze sits over ground, under men). Gate at `cam.scale <= 22` — a haze band is meaningless when you can count boots — and drop to a single band below 6 px/m. Add a `?haze=0` query flag matching the existing `?fow=0` pattern so scripts/sweep.mjs can shoot with and without.

DUST MOTES: at `cam.scale >= 20`, 24 motes positioned from `hash(Math.floor(wx/7), Math.floor(wy/7), i)` so they stay anchored to the world and do not swim when the camera pans; drifting on WIND with a wrapping phase; `blit('dustTan', r = 0.04 m, alpha 0.10)`. Twenty-four sub-pixel-adjacent specks is enough to stop close-in shots reading as a flat vector diagram.

WIND-LEAN THE EXISTING SMOKE: `drawSmoke` (renderer.ts:246-272) drifts each puff purely radially with a `spin` term and no prevailing direction, so a smoke screen billows like a flower instead of streaming. Add `+ WIND.dx * WIND.speed * 0.35 * elapsed` and the `dy` equivalent to each puff's world position — critically, derive it from `elapsed` (which comes from the sim-owned ttl), NOT from `now`, so smoke screens stay frozen under pause exactly as the file's header comment demands.

STARTLED BIRDS: in `addBooms`, if any tile within 7 m of the boom has `terrainKeyAt === 'woods'`, push 3-6 birds `{ x, y, dir, at, phase }`. Each bird is two short strokes (`rgba(38,34,28,0.75)`, lineWidth `Math.max(1, cam.scale*0.035)`) forming a chevron whose half-angle flaps on `Math.sin(now*0.022 + phase)`, flying `dir` at 11 m/s for 1900 ms with a rising offset `t*3.5*cam.scale` and a ground shadow ellipse fading as it climbs. Wall-clock, `fxDetail >= 1`, hard cap 24 live. Six primitives per bird, at most ~150 strokes on a heavy frame — the cheapest 'this world is alive' beat available.
tasks.risks: Haze is a fill-rate cost on top of an already-composited scene; bands keep it to 5 drawImages but verify the >=100 fps floor at 247 soldiers with haze ON at scale 12 (the worst case: many bands visible AND many sprites). Haze alpha above ~0.08 will flatten the value separation the whole art direction is built on — this is a milk-glass risk, tune down not up. Birds triggered by every boom in a wooded map could fire constantly during a barrage; the 24 cap plus a per-boom 1-in-2 hash gate handles it.

tasks.title: Extend the vfx.mjs regression gate and shot.mjs inspector to cover every new effect
tasks.detail:
Without this, most of FX2-FX7 lands outside the gate and silently regresses.

BLOCKING HARNESS DEFECT: `stage.mjs:172` pushes `{fx, fy, tx, ty, hit, kill}` with NO `weapon` field, so every per-class flash path added in FX3 would be untested and the gate would only ever exercise the `weapon === undefined` → cannon fallback. Change `burst()` to pass `weapon` and `shooterId` through from `trigger`, and `r` through for booms (`sim.pendingBooms.push({ x, y, r: trigger.r })`).

NEW DYNAMIC ROWS in `vfx.mjs` DYN: `muzzle mg42` (weapon:'mg42' — catches the double-beat), `muzzle thompson`, `muzzle bazooka` (the back-blast cone is the whole point), `cannon blast` (weapon:'pak40_gun'), `grenade boom` (r:3), `barrage boom` (r:9), `wall strike` (a miss staged 3 m off a building edge so the FX4 overshoot ray lands on masonry — derive the anchor from `deriveTargets(...).village` and offset toward a known wall), `ricochet`. Bucket counts: flashes 4 buckets over 140 ms (the current 6-over-340 wastes half its buckets on an empty tail for short effects); booms 8 buckets over 2600 ms.

BUMP THE SETTLE WAIT: `vfx.mjs:58` waits 2200 ms for booms to expire before the static captures, sized to the old BOOM_MS=2000. FX2 extends the smoke column to 2600 ms — raise to 2800 or the death-pose shot gets photobombed.

NEW STATIC ROWS (pause-safe, plain `page.screenshot`): `building fire` (push a boom on a building tile, wait 2.8 s for the transient to clear, shoot the fire — its lifetime is sim-tick driven so it survives the pause, which is the point of the FX5 clock split and worth asserting); `casings` (12 mg42 shots at scale 40, wait 600 ms for the hops to land, shoot the brass); `pockmarks` (20 misses into one wall, shoot the spread); `death pose boom` and `death pose melee` (set `deathCause` + `deathDirX/Y` then `alive = false`, same rAF dance as the existing death-pose row); `haze` (a `?haze=1` far shot at scale 12).

SCORING: keep `peak.score > 40` for the loud effects. Casings and pockmarks are deliberately quiet and will fail that bar — give those rows a tightened ROI (shrink `roiFrac` to 0.25 around the anchor) or a per-row `minPeak` of 15, and set it per row rather than weakening the global assertion.

`shot.mjs` EFFECTS map: add `mg`, `bazooka`, `grenade`, `barrage`, `wall`, `fire` so any agent (including the pi harness) can eyeball a single effect in one shell command.
tasks.risks: Cheap but load-bearing — do it in the same session as FX2/FX3, not after, or the intervening commits land unverified. Adding rows lengthens the gate run; keep the total under a few minutes or people stop running it. The 1-in-5 tracer-round hash gate from FX3 means shot rows must be staged at fixed coordinates or the captured frame flickers between tracer and no-tracer across runs and reads as a regression.

terrain.summary: Current ground art is a competent flat base with almost no micro-detail: grass is a 2×2 sub-tile value fill plus 5 hash speckles per tile (no direction, no tufts, no flowers), roads are a flat fill with 2 dark dots, 4 straight shoulder strips and two dead-straight per-tile rut rects, fields are one fill plus axis-aligned furrow lines whose phase/orientation resets on every 8 m block (visible as graph-paper patchwork in base-farm), woods floor is 4 ellipses, and trees are a single circle + one highlight circle + dark stroke, which is why base-woods reads as bubble wrap. There is no clutter layer at all — nothing man-made anywhere except hedge capsules and buildings, so base-bocage/base-village read as empty lawn with buildings dropped on it and no village paving, kerbs, fences, poles or yard props. The detail that does exist is drawn identically at every zoom band, so it is wasted work at band 4-8 and starved at band 32-48. Measured on this machine (headless Chrome, getImageData-flushed): a 16×16 chunk bake costs 4.0-5.2 ms and is essentially band-independent — call-count bound, not fill-rate bound (fillRect ≈0.5 µs, arc+fill ≈2.3 µs, drawImage ≈1.3 µs at band 48) — and a zoom step across a band boundary (e.g. 8→9 px/m) invalidates the whole cache keyspace and needs ~70 fresh chunk bakes for a 1280×800 viewport, i.e. a ~300 ms stall today. Any detail increase multiplies that stall, so the first task must be per-band detail tiers + pre-baked detail stamps (≈10 shapes for the price of 1.3 µs) + a per-frame bake budget with coarse-band fallback; everything after that is content, all of it derivable from GameMap alone (tiles/buildingId/bridges/elev) with zero src/sim changes.

tasks.title: Detail-LOD tiers, stamp atlas, and bake budget with coarse-band fallback
tasks.detail:
Foundation for every other task — land first.

(a) Detail tiers. In terrain.ts add `type Detail = 0 | 1 | 2` and `const detailFor = (band: number): Detail => (band >= 32 ? 2 : band >= 16 ? 1 : 0);`. Compute once in `chunk()` and thread `d` through `drawTileBase`, `drawTree`, `drawHedgeRun`, `drawSubTileGround` and the new passes. Gate existing work: grass 5-speckle loop and road pothole arcs → `d >= 1`; woods 4 litter ellipses → replaced by a litter stamp at `d >= 1`; field furrows stay at all tiers (they are the readable macro structure) but drop to ≤1 row/tile at d=0. Net effect at band 4-8: fewer ops than today and a cleaner far-LOD (base-farlod must stay pixel-similar).

(b) `src/render/stamps.ts` — pre-baked detail patches, the cost lever. API: `export function stamp(key: string, band: number, size: number, draw: (g: CanvasRenderingContext2D) => void): HTMLCanvasElement`. Module-level `Map<string, HTMLCanvasElement>` keyed `${key}:${band}` (callers fold variant/axis into `key`); canvas is `size*band` px square; inside, `g.scale(band); g.lineCap='round'` so the draw callback works in meters over 0..size. Callers blit `g.drawImage(c, x, y, size, size)` — the chunk ctx is scaled by band and translated by whole tiles, so dest maps 1:1 to source pixels: crisp, no resample. Track total cached pixels, cap at 8_000_000 and `console.warn` on overflow (typical usage: ~24 grass + 8 litter + 8 gravel + 6 cobble variants × 5 bands ≈ 1.5 M px). Never call `Math.random` here — every stamp's content comes from `hash(variant, 0, salt)`.

(c) Bake budget + fallback. `TerrainLayer` gains `private bakeBudget = 0;` set to 2 at the top of `draw()`. `chunk(cx, cy, band)` → `chunk(cx, cy, band, mayBake: boolean)`; on a miss with `bakeBudget <= 0`, return null and have `draw()` call a new `blitFallback(ctx, cx, cy, sx, sy, size)` that walks BANDS from highest to lowest looking for any cached `${cx},${cy},${b}` and blits it with that band's own source rect (`drawImage(c, b, b, CHUNK*b, CHUNK*b, sx, sy, size, size)`); prefer higher bands (crisper) over lower. If nothing is cached, fill a per-chunk average tone from a `Uint8Array` of mean TERRAIN colors computed in the ctor (one pass over map.tiles) so a fresh region never flashes the `#161510` backdrop. Decrement `bakeBudget` on each real bake.

(d) `scripts/bake.mjs` — perf gate, reuses `launch()` from scripts/lib/stage.mjs. In-page: `generateMap(seed,320,240,'town')`, build a fresh `TerrainLayer` per measurement (so the LRU never warms), time `layer['chunk'](cx,cy,band)` followed by `getContext('2d').getImageData(0,0,1,1)` to force rasterization; 5 reps averaged; chunks = village crossroads, densest-hedge chunk, densest-woods chunk; bands 8/16/32/48. Print a table and exit 1 if any average exceeds 8 ms. Baseline to record in the plan doc: village 4.x, bocage ~4.5, woods 4.0-5.2 ms today.
tasks.risks: Fallback blits can show a chunk at the wrong sharpness for a few frames (acceptable — same content, and it replaces a hard stall). Getting the fallback source-rect band wrong produces visibly offset terrain; the gutter is 1 tile = `band` px on every side, so the src origin is always `(b, b)`. The stamp 1:1 pixel mapping only holds while chunk `translate` is whole tiles — do not introduce fractional tile translates.

tasks.title: Grass micro-detail: mowing-direction mottling, tuft-cluster stamps, wildflower meadows
tasks.detail:
Depends on G1. Grass is the single largest surface on screen and currently the flattest.

(a) noise.ts additions (keep `hash` untouched): `export function vec(x, y, salt, cell): [number, number]` — per-lattice angle `hash(ix,iy,salt)*Math.PI`, bilinearly interpolate cos and sin separately (never the angle — wrap artifacts), lattice `cell` in meters. Plus `export function fine(x, y, salt = 3): number` — bilinear value noise on a 2 m lattice for sub-tile mottling. Use `vec(x, y, 205, 34)` as the mowing/wind direction field: only its dominant axis is consumed (`Math.abs(dx) > Math.abs(dy) ? 'ew' : 'ns'`), so all stamps stay axis-aligned and crisp.

(b) Tuft stamps. 12 variants × 2 axes, 1 m, key `grass:${v}:${axis}`: 14-20 tapered strokes grouped into 3-4 clumps (clump centers from `hash(v,0,206..)`), lineWidth 0.03-0.055, length 0.10-0.22 m, oriented ±20° around the stamp axis, values `shade(GRASS,1.22)`, `shade(GRASS,0.72)`, `shade(GRASS_DRY,1.10)`, plus 2 dark contact ticks (`rgba(18,22,14,0.25)`, 0.05 m) at clump bases so tufts sit on the ground rather than float. Keep all geometry inside 0.05..0.95 m so no stamp bleeds and the 1 m lattice never becomes visible; the anti-lattice guarantee comes from variant + mirrored variants (bake 4 pre-flipped copies rather than using ctx transforms).

(c) Per-tile use in `drawTileBase` grass branch: keep the 2×2 sub-tile value fill (it is the value base and must stay), delete the 5-rect speckle loop, and at `d >= 1` blit one tuft stamp: `const v = (hash(x,y,201) * 12) | 0` and axis from the flow field. At `d >= 1` also add the mottling that reads as mown stripes/wind combing: bake it INTO the stamp (3 elongated soft rects, 0.5-0.9 m long × 0.10-0.18 m, alpha 0.05-0.09, alternating lighter/darker along the stamp axis) so per-tile cost stays one drawImage (~1.3 µs) instead of ~8 fillRects.

(d) Wildflower meadows at `d >= 2` only: `const bloom = macro(x + 411, y + 87) > 0.63` (offset lattice = flower patches uncorrelated with the grass hue drift; ≈12% of grass tiles). Bloom tiles use 4 extra stamp variants keyed `grass:bloom:${v}:${axis}` that add 5-9 dots of 0.03-0.05 m in cream `rgba(228,224,198,0.60)`, pale ochre `rgba(208,188,122,0.50)`, dusty mauve `rgba(162,142,158,0.45)` — desaturated per the palette rule; nothing hot.

(e) Road verge upgrade (keeps the existing dusty verge rects): at `d >= 1`, on grass tiles adjacent to road, 3-5 tufts leaning over the road edge (blit a 0.35 m `grass:verge:${v}` stamp on the road side) plus 2 bare-earth patches `rgba(146,122,84,0.22)` of 0.15-0.3 m — this softens the razor-straight road edge visible in base-village/base-farm from the grass side (G3 does the road side).

Salt range for this task: 200-219 (existing terrain salts occupy 1-9, 30-45, 54-73, 80-97, 110, 120-151).
tasks.risks: Over-detailing at band 16 can read as noise at mid zoom — validate the bocage crop at 16 px/m as well as 48. Flower dots must stay under the ~35% saturation ceiling and must not appear at d<2 (a sweep validator has already once misread small red dots as poppies). Do not let tuft strokes cross the 1 m stamp edge or the tuft lattice becomes a visible grid, violating rule 3.

tasks.title: Road wear pass: continuous wobbling ruts, potholes with puddle glints, crumbled edges, gravel
tasks.detail:
Depends on G1. Roads are the strongest lines in the frame and currently the most synthetic: two straight per-tile rects for ruts, a hard 0.12 m shoulder, and an axis inference (`w || e`) that is simply wrong at junctions and corners.

(a) New post-pass `drawRoadWear(g, map, tx0, ty0, tx1, ty1, d)` called from `chunk()` after the tile-base loop and before `drawWaterBanks` (same architecture as `drawHedgeRun` — wear must be continuous across tile and chunk seams). For each road tile that is not a bridge, build segments from the tile center to each orthogonal road neighbor's center, offset perpendicular by ±0.26 m with a smooth lateral wobble `(coarse(x*3, y*3) - 0.5) * 0.18` applied to both endpoints — segment-per-neighbor is what makes runs continuous and corner-correct. Three stroke passes over the whole segment list (layer at a time, as hedges do): body `rgba(58,44,30,0.16)` w=0.13, core `rgba(40,30,20,0.10)` w=0.06, then a NW dust lip `rgba(196,172,120,0.10)` w=0.05 offset by (-0.05,-0.06) so the groove reads as a depression under the one sun. Junction tiles (3+ road neighbors) get no ruts; instead two turning arcs r=0.7 and r=1.1 centered on the junction's inner corner, `rgba(52,40,26,0.12)`, w=0.12. Delete the current rut rects from the road branch of `drawTileBase`.

(b) Crown: a 0.06 m line along the run at `rgba(184,160,112,0.08)` between the ruts — cheap and reads as a crowned dirt lane.

(c) Potholes at `d >= 1`: `hash(x,y,230) < 0.13` → ellipse rx 0.10-0.22, ry 0.7·rx, core `rgba(34,26,18,0.40)` with a NW rim `rgba(150,126,86,0.25)` offset (-0.03,-0.035). At `d >= 2` and `hash(x,y,231) < 0.05` fill it as a puddle: `rgba(92,104,104,0.50)` body + a NW crescent glint `rgba(228,232,224,0.30)` (arc 200°→320°, w=0.04). This is the only specular in the scene and it must point at the same NW sun.

(d) Edge crumble replacing the four straight shoulder rects: for each non-road edge, 4 sub-steps of 0.25 m with depth `0.06 + hash(x*4+i, y, 232) * 0.14`, drawn first in road-dark `rgba(0,0,0,0.15)` then the existing dust-tan `rgba(168,140,92,0.12)` following the crumbled depth, plus 2 scallops of 0.18-0.22 m biting inward from the verge in the grass tone. Result: no more perfectly straight road boundary.

(e) Aggregate at `d >= 2`: `road:gravel:${v}` 1 m stamps, 8 variants, 12-16 specks of 0.025-0.045 m in bone `rgba(198,186,158,0.35)`, dark `rgba(44,36,26,0.30)`, mid `rgba(120,102,74,0.30)`; one blit per road tile.

Stacked-darkness discipline: total added dark alpha on a road tile must stay ≤0.25 or the arterial goes muddy at mid zoom — check the village@12 and farlod@3.5 crops for value drift.
tasks.risks: Wear must not draw on bridge tiles (`map.isBridge`) — the plank deck owns that surface. The road-axis logic must handle 1-tile-wide lanes carved by farm compounds (a single road tile with one neighbor gets a stub rut, which is correct). Do not let ruts run through paving added in G7 — gate on the G7 paved predicate.

tasks.title: Render-side patch index, then real crop rows: parcel-wide row angle, lit furrow ridges, headlands
tasks.detail:
Depends on G1. Also the data dependency for G6 and G7. All derived from GameMap — no src/sim edits.

(a) `src/render/patches.ts`: `export class PatchIndex { readonly id: Int16Array; readonly patches: {kind: TerrainKey; tiles: number; minX: number; minY: number; maxX: number; maxY: number; cx: number; cy: number; seed: number}[]; readonly junctions: {x: number; y: number; degree: number; buildings: number}[]; constructor(map: GameMap) }`. 4-connected flood fill over `field` and `woods` tiles only (grass is one region and needs no id); `seed = hash(minX, minY, 240) * 65536 | 0`. Junctions: road tiles with ≥3 orthogonal road neighbors, clustered within 3 m (keep the cluster centroid), each annotated with the count of distinct `map.buildingIdAt` values within 22 m. Building footprints come free from `buildingId` — add `readonly buildings: {id: number; minX: number; minY: number; maxX: number; maxY: number}[]` derived in the same pass. Cost: one O(w·h) pass = 76,800 tiles on a 320×240 map, ~1 ms at map load; construct it once in the `TerrainLayer` ctor and expose it (G6/G7 consume the same instance).

(b) Field rows keyed on the PARCEL, not the 8 m block — this is the fix for the graph-paper look in base-farm where adjacent blocks disagree on furrow direction. From `patch.seed`: `angle = (hash(seed,0,241) - 0.5) * 0.5 + (hash(seed,0,242) < 0.5 ? 0 : Math.PI/2)` (rows within ±14° of an axis — a slight diagonal is what reads agricultural), `spacing = 0.34 + hash(seed,0,243) * 0.36`, phase measured from the parcel centroid so rows are continuous over the entire parcel.

(c) Per-tile row drawing without clip(): for the row indices whose lines intersect the unit square, compute the line `n·p = c` with `n = (Math.sin(a), -Math.cos(a))` and clip the segment to the tile with a 4-plane parametric clip (~10 lines of math), then one moveTo/lineTo per row. 3-5 rows/tile at `d >= 1`, 1 at d=0. No clip, no overdraw, no per-tile save/restore.

(d) Crop type from `hash(seed,0,244)`: plowed 0.40 / cereal 0.35 / roots 0.25, each driving GEOMETRY not just hue:
- plowed: trough stroke `rgba(38,28,18,0.22)` w=0.10 plus a ridge highlight `rgba(196,176,132,0.13)` w=0.06 offset NW by (-0.045,-0.055) → genuine corrugation lit by the shared sun. Biggest single payoff in the task.
- cereal: base tone biased to the wheat FIELD_VARIANT, row stroke `rgba(178,160,104,0.18)`; at `d >= 2` a `field:stubble:${v}` stamp (short 0.06 m dashes along rows) and a darker tramline every 12th row.
- roots: dark-green rosettes every 0.42 m along each row, r 0.05-0.07 m, two values `rgba(74,92,52,0.55)` / `rgba(52,68,40,0.5)`, jitter from `hash(x*7+i, y, 245)`.

(e) Headlands: on parcel-border tiles (any non-field 4-neighbor) draw the outer 0.5 m of rows PARALLEL to that border and add a 0.25 m bare turning strip `rgba(112,94,62,0.18)`; keep the existing dark boundary strip. Real fields turn at the edge and this is what makes a parcel read as farmed rather than hatched.

(f) `tests/patches.test.ts` (pure, no canvas — vitest runs in node): over 10 seeds assert every field/woods tile has an id ≥ 0, every patch's tiles are 4-connected, ids are stable across two constructions of the same map, ≥1 junction is found within 3 m of mapgen's crossroads, and building footprints match `map.buildingIdAt` bounds.
tasks.risks: Parcel floods can be large (a 26×18 field patch) — the row phase must be derived from the centroid, not from the tile, or rows drift between chunks. Diagonal rows at d=0 will alias into moiré at band 4-8; force axis-aligned single rows at d=0. Orchard tiles are `woods` patches with holes — G5 must not treat every small woods patch as an orchard without the stagger test.

tasks.title: Canopy sprite set (lobed silhouette, NW-lit, deep SE shade), orchard variant, woods-floor litter and logs, hedge foliage depth + earth bank
tasks.risks: Sprite memory: 3 m at band 48 = 144² × 12 variants × 3 families ≈ 750 k px — inside the stamps cap, but re-check the cap when G2/G3 stamps are also resident. Scaling a 3 m sprite by k introduces resample blur for non-integer k; quantize k to 1/8 steps so the same source rect scale repeats and stays predictable. Hedge silhouette dabs must not cross into a neighbor tile's mass darkly or per-tile segmentation returns — verify bocage at 16 and 48 px/m.

tasks.title: Environmental clutter: haystacks, carts, barrels, wells, troughs, muck heaps, fence lines, telegraph poles, weathered old craters
tasks.detail:
Depends on G1 + G4. The single biggest 'this is a real place' lever: there is currently zero man-made clutter anywhere.

(a) `src/render/props.ts`: `export type PropKind = 'haystack'|'cart'|'barrels'|'crates'|'well'|'trough'|'muckheap'|'fencepost'|'gate'|'telegraph';` `export interface Prop { x: number; y: number; kind: PropKind; seed: number; axis: 0 | 1 }` and a PURE `export function propsFor(map: GameMap, patches: PatchIndex): Prop[]` plus `export function drawProp(g: Ctx, p: Prop, band: number, d: Detail): void`. Build the list once in the `TerrainLayer` ctor and bucket it into `Map<string, Prop[]>` by chunk key (a prop is added to every chunk whose tile range + pad its footprint touches) so a chunk bake pays only for its own props (~10-40 blits ≈ 0.05 ms). Draw them in `chunk()` after hedges/trees, before `drawEdge`. Salts 260-299.

(b) Legality gate `canPlace` (props are decoration with no sim collision, so keep them off tiles that matter): terrain must be grass or field for freestanding props; road props sit on the grass/field VERGE tile next to the road, never the running surface; never floor, water, hedge or bridge; never within 1 m of a DOOR edge (door trails own that); never inside a building footprint (wall-huggers sit on the outside face); minimum 0.8 m between props.

(c) Placement rules and geometry (each ≤12 ops; haystack/telegraph/fencepost get stamps since they repeat):
- haystack: cereal parcels (G4 crop type), 1 per 60 parcel tiles, ≥3 tiles inside the parcel — base ellipse `#8a7440` r≈0.9, 3 thatch arcs brightening toward NW, cap `rgba(206,186,130,0.55)`, SE shadow lobe at `shadowOffset(2.2)` alpha 0.30, AO ring.
- cart: farm yards (building pairs from `patches.buildings` whose footprints are ≤4 m apart) and square edges — bed = 2 plank rects `#6e5a3c`/`#5a4830` 2.2×1.1 m, 4 wheel rings r 0.22 `#3a2f22` with 2 crossing spokes, 2 shaft strokes, SE shadow rect.
- barrels / crates: 1-3 hugging a building's N or W exterior face — barrel = circle r 0.25 `#5a4a34` + NW rim crescent `rgba(190,176,140,0.25)` + AO; crate = 0.7 m rounded rect with plank lines + SE shadow.
- well: 1 per settlement (junction cluster with ≥4 buildings within 22 m) or farm yard — stone ring of 8 jittered quads, dark interior circle, 2 posts + beam with SE shadows, bucket dot.
- trough: farm yard, 1.6×0.5 m dark rect + `rgba(92,104,104,0.50)` water + NW glint.
- muckheap: farm yard, 5 overlapping `#4a3c26` lobes + straw flecks + AO.
- fencepost/gate: parcel borders (G4) with no hedge tile that face a road or lane — posts every 1.6 m (0.10×0.14 m dark rect + a 0.5 m SE shadow strip alpha 0.16) with 2 rails `rgba(96,80,56,0.70)` w=0.05 drawn 0.35/0.55 m 'above' the post base to fake height; a 2-diagonal-rail gate at the lane opening. This is what gives base-bocage man-made structure where hedges are absent.
- telegraph: verge of straight road runs (≥6 tiles on one axis), every 6 m along the run — 0.22 m dark base + trunk ellipse, 0.9 m crossarm, 2 insulator dots `rgba(198,190,166,0.50)`, a 2.6 m tapered SE shadow strip alpha 0.18, and at `d >= 1` the forward wire to the NEXT pole only (quadratic sag 0.35 m, `rgba(30,28,24,0.22)`, w=0.03). Wires cross chunks: raise the chunk `pad` from 2 to 3 and keep pole spacing at 6 m so a per-pole forward segment is always fully covered by overscan. Cost: 400→484 tiles per chunk (+21% bake) — re-run scripts/bake.mjs and confirm ≤8 ms.
- old craters (shell-crater-ready): 0-6 per map, weathered, placed near junctions and patch centroids, stamped into `DecalLayer` at construction via a new `oldCrater(x, y, seed)` (rim with grass regrowth `rgba(96,110,66,0.25)`, core `rgba(40,34,26,0.35)`, no ash) so fresh `scorch()` marks still read as new. Renderer calls it in a ctor loop over `propsFor`-adjacent crater picks.

(d) Tier gating: at d=0 draw silhouette + shadow only (one dark lobe + base color) so far zoom shows readable specks, not mush; full detail at `d >= 1`.

(e) `tests/props.test.ts` (pure, no canvas): over 10 seeds — no prop on a road/floor/water/hedge/bridge tile, none within 1 m of a door, total count within 120..500 on 320×240, byte-identical list across two builds of the same map, and no two props within 0.8 m.
tasks.risks: Props have no collision (src/sim is off-limits), so soldiers will walk through a haystack — mitigate by keeping large props off the road surface, off doorway tiles, and ≥2 m from building walls except the wall-huggers. The pad 2→3 bump raises every chunk bake ~21%; it must land together with G1's budget or high-zoom panning hitches. Telegraph wires drawn from both a pole's own chunk and its neighbour's overscan will each be correct but are drawn twice on different canvases — harmless; a wire drawn with the WRONG next-pole (list order not sorted along the run) shows as a zigzag.

tasks.title: Village square and courtyard paving: cobbles with alpha ramp, kerbs, gutters, packed-earth yards, building aprons
tasks.detail:
Depends on G1 + G4. base-village currently has buildings sitting on plain dirt-road and grass with no civic surface at all.

(a) Square detection (no sim access needed — battle-map objectives are not on Sim, so derive it): from `patches.junctions`, a square is a junction cluster with ≥4 distinct building ids within 22 m; `r = 8 + 0.4 * min(6, buildingsWithin22m)` clamped to 8..11 m. Store `squares: {cx, cy, r}[]` on PatchIndex. The ≥4-buildings requirement is load-bearing — it keeps a lone farm lane junction from being paved.

(b) Cobbles: `village:cobble:${v}` 1 m stamps, 6 variants — a 4×4 lattice of 0.22 m quads with ±0.05 m corner jitter, 4 desaturated grey-tan stone values around `[134,126,112]` (±10%), joints `rgba(40,34,26,0.35)` at 0.03 m, and a per-stone NW top-edge highlight `rgba(206,198,176,0.18)` on the two NW edges so each stone catches the same sun. Applied to road tiles and road-adjacent grass tiles inside `r`, blitted over the road base. Avoid a hard paving ring with a per-tile alpha ramp: `const a = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, (r - dist) / 3)); g.globalAlpha = a; ...blit...; g.globalAlpha = 1;` (one property set, cheaper than baking alpha variants). Suppress G3 ruts/gravel where `a > 0.5`.

(c) Kerb: on each paved tile edge meeting unpaved grass/field, a 0.10 m strip `rgba(158,150,132,0.50)` plus a 0.04 m base line `rgba(30,26,20,0.30)` on the outer side — gives the square a hard civic boundary and reads correctly at 12 px/m.

(d) Gutter: along the road run inside the square, 0.06 m dark lines at ±0.42 m from the run center with a dust rim `rgba(184,160,112,0.08)` — French village crown-and-gutter profile.

(e) Farm courtyard: for building pairs ≤4 m apart (mapgen's house+barn share a yard row), blend the tiles between them toward packed earth `[128,110,80]` at `alpha = 0.35 * (1 - dist/2)`, plus 3-6 straw flecks and 2 wheel-scuff arcs `rgba(70,56,36,0.14)`; existing door trails draw on top.

(f) Building apron: a 0.6 m gravel band outside every exterior wall from `patches.buildings` bounds — `rgba(150,138,112,0.22)` with speckle at `d >= 2`, drawn under the existing wall AO so buildings stop growing straight out of lawn.

Draw order inside `chunk()`: tile bases → road wear (G3) → paving/apron/courtyard (this task) → kerb → water banks → door trails → hedges → trees → props → edges → hillshade.
tasks.risks: Paving that extends onto grass tiles must respect the alpha ramp or the square gets a visible circular edge (rule 3). globalAlpha around a blit is cheap but must be reset on every path — a leaked globalAlpha tints the rest of the chunk. Cobble stones at band 8 collapse into mush; gate the stamp to `d >= 1` and use a flat paving tone at d=0. Verify the village@12 and village-roofs@8 crops plus farlod@3.5 for value drift.

tasks.title: Extend the art regression gate for the new ground detail
tasks.detail:
Do last (or land the bake.mjs half with G1). The existing sweep shoots 8 crops × 10 seeds at mid zooms, so it is nearly blind to the tiers this work introduces.

(a) Add three crops to the sweep target set in scripts/lib/stage.mjs `deriveTargets`: `groundclose` — a grass/road boundary tile at scale 48 (pick the road tile nearest the village with ≥2 grass neighbors, offset 1.5 m into the grass); `fieldclose` — a cereal parcel centroid at scale 32; `squareclose` — the detected village square center at scale 24. These are the three surfaces where d=2 detail lives; without them nothing regression-covers tuft stamps, puddle glints, crop rosettes or cobbles.

(b) Add a band-boundary pair to the sweep: the same scene at scale 15 and scale 17 (band 16 vs band 32). Any detail that pops discontinuously across a band change is a bug — this catches tier-gating mistakes that a single-scale crop cannot.

(c) Land scripts/bake.mjs from G1 as a standing perf gate and document the thresholds next to the sweep in the plan doc: per-chunk bake ≤8 ms at every band on village/bocage/woods chunks; record today's measured baseline (4.0-5.2 ms, band-independent, getImageData-flushed) and the post-pad-bump expectation (+21% from pad 2→3). Note the measured per-op costs at band 48 (fillRect 0.5 µs, arc+fill 2.3 µs, drawImage 1.3 µs) so future art work reaches for stamps instead of arcs by default.

(d) Also re-run the in-browser fps spot check at 247 soldiers (the ≥100 fps floor) while panning at scale 48 across un-baked chunks — that pan is the only situation where the bake budget is exercised, and it is exactly what the sweep's static frames cannot see.
tasks.risks: New crops invalidate nothing but will make the contact sheet wider — regenerate the baseline sheet in the same commit or every later diff reads as a regression. The band-boundary pair is sensitive to camera rounding; pin both shots to the same world center so only `scale` differs.
